提示词：

【主题】：
【中文标题】：
【英文标题】：
【核心主体】：
【左右关系】：巨物压场 / 图像窄带 × 宽文字场 / 主体 × 档案 / 图像越界 / 密集 × 留白 / 其他
【左侧内容】：
【右侧内容】：
【跨界元素】：器物轮廓 / 枝叶 / 大字 / 线稿 / 纹样 / 其他
【主色调】：
【强调色】：
【日期 / 场馆】：
【画面比例】：9:16

生成一张高审美、高信息密度的东方文化展览海报，采用「左右构图 / 非对称双区构图」。

左右不要 50 / 50 平均切开，根据主体体量、文字密度和留白关系灵活使用 35 / 65、40 / 60、45 / 55 等比例。重点不是两侧面积相等，而是让图像重量、Typography 和信息密度达到视觉平衡。

根据主题灵活选择不同方式：

巨物压场：一侧放大尺度器物、文物或艺术对象，允许大胆裁切，占据主要视觉重量；另一侧通过标题、英文、小字、结构线稿和展讯建立阅读层级。

图像窄带 × 宽文字场：一侧使用修长古画、摄影或纹样切片，另一侧保留更大的纸面与 Typography。图像中的枝叶、飞鸟、云气或主体轮廓可主动越出画芯进入文字区。

主体 × 档案：一侧保持单一强主体，另一侧组合器型线稿、材质微距、拓片、纹样研究、尺寸、年代和少量说明文字，形成艺术图录感。

密集 × 留白：一侧通过图像、档案碎片和研究内容形成高密度视觉，另一侧保持大面积控制过的留白，只使用少量大字和关键展讯。留白不能只是“没有内容”，要通过字距、细线、位置和比例被精确设计。

左右边界不要过于机械。可以让器物边缘、大字、花枝、纹样或研究线条跨过分界约 3%–10%，把两侧重新连接起来，但避免随意拼贴。

Typography 必须根据每张画面的主体重新设计。可以使用超大单字、两字错位、完整横排标题、中等尺度标题、跨栏文字或局部反色。坚持“大字很大、小字很小”的尺度反差，减少无意义的中号字。不要固定使用四字纵排，也不要重复“两字横排 + 两字竖排”的模板。

信息密度参考成熟博物馆海报、Japanese Editorial Design 和 Art Catalogue。可加入英文副标题、年代、材质、工艺、场馆、日期、策展短句，以及 1–3 个与主题直接相关的研究节点，例如器型线稿、釉面微距、古画材料、纹样拓片、石纹研究或局部放大。

这些辅助信息必须服务主题，不要为了“显得专业”而堆随机小字。

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色。优先使用骨白、墨黑、青瓷绿、石青石绿、深灰、赭色等克制色彩，再加入一个明确但面积很小的朱砂红或其他强调色。纸面保持干净，不使用脏黄仿古滤镜。

第一眼看到大型主体与左右重量关系；第二眼看到标题和主要色块；第三眼发现器物、古画或枝叶如何突破左右边界；最后再阅读材质、结构、年代与展览档案。

核心原则：一边负责压住视觉，一边负责承接阅读；留白也是重量，信息密度也是重量；左右不相等，但整体必须平衡。

整体要求：9:16，高清、清晰、纸面干净、主体质感真实、Typography 锐利、细线与小字尽可能清楚，信息丰富但不乱，具有成熟博物馆海报和艺术出版物完成度。

避免：机械五五分、简单左图右字、左右各放一个相似主体、主体过小、信息区像说明书、固定标题模板、PPT 信息框、复杂 UI、随机英文、严重做旧、斑驳噪点、画面编号、版权标识、四角星芒、sparkle 和低完成度 AI 海报感。

Autumn in my hair, a leaf in my hand.

Prompt: 
Do not change the face, facial features or body proportions at all. Do not use the clothing from the reference.

Vertical, extremely close-up, ultra-photorealistic natural selfie. Tight crop; face, hair and upper body almost completely fill the frame. Camera is directly in front, at face level and very slightly above. No posed or studio-shot feeling.

The woman is comfortably half-reclining against a wooden backrest, torso slightly angled. Her head is noticeably tilted toward her shoulder and turned in a slight 3/4 view. One arm is raised above her head with the elbow bent; the forearm is at the top edge of the frame. Her hand rests in her hair, fingers slightly curled, holding a yellow maple leaf. Short square French manicure and a diamond silver ring on her wrist.

Hair falls below the waist — incredibly thick, luxurious voluminous layered blowout: strong volume at the roots, large flowing S-waves/curls and heavy silky layers. A wide front section falls diagonally across the face, partially covering one eye.

Playful direct gaze at the camera through her hair; eyes slightly narrowed, lips slightly parted, faint half-smile.

Oversized brown, dark-brown and black plaid shirt with the top buttons undone, a silver cross-pendant necklace visible. Over it she wears an expensive-looking dark brown vest.

Hard, direct warm golden-hour sunlight coming from the side / slightly above. Strong highlights on the center of the face, skin, hand and some hair strands; deep graphic shadows in the hand, hair and fabric folds. One side of the face is bright, the other side heavily shadowed. Autumn trees in the background; artificially blur the background.

Keep natural skin texture, visible pores, micro-imperfections and fine capillaries in the eyes. No perfect facial symmetry. Skin even and matte with wet-look highlighter on cheekbones, nose tip and bridge; light contour. Full, tinted laminated brows; dense fox-eye lashes; slightly glossy, defined lips.

Unprocessed RAW photo aesthetic; natural smartphone exposure, slight overexposed areas in the sun, realistic skin/hair texture, natural fabric folds, light film grain and digital noise. No beauty filter, CGI, flash, HDR, plastic skin or heavy retouching. Subsurface scattering, Tyndall effect and hyper-detailed irises. Photorealism that combines iPhone 16/17 Pro Max naturalness with the detail of a Fujifilm GFX 100 + 100 mm lens, 8K.  
Aspect ratio: 3:4.

prompts.text:
Prompt:

Create a bold editorial campaign poster where oversized typography works like an optical tool and visibly changes the subject or scene.

Brand: [BRAND NAME]
Product / Campaign: [PRODUCT OR CAMPAIGN]
Main Word: [SHORT WORD]
Subject: [PERSON / PRODUCT / BOTH]
Optical Effect: [FOCUS / ZOOM / REFRACT / PRISM / OTHER]
Main Color: [COLOR]
Accent Color: [COLOR]
Aspect Ratio: [9:16]

Use realistic commercial photography, oversized typography, strong high-contrast colors, and contemporary editorial design.

Make the main word extremely large and let it perform a clear optical function:

 FOCUS: shift parts of the subject from soft blur into sharp focus.
 ZOOM: use a letter or its negative space as a lens that naturally magnifies the subject.
 REFRACT: use transparent letterforms to slightly bend, shift, or distort the image behind them.
 PRISM: let light pass through the typography and split into a few controlled colors.

The optical effect should physically interact with the person or product while keeping faces, bodies, and product structures realistic and intact.

Create clear foreground, subject, and background layering, with some typography passing behind the subject and other parts entering the foreground.

Use one dominant high-impact color with black, white, and one or two controlled accent colors. Add only a few meaningful campaign details such as the brand name, product name, slogan, specs, or small editorial labels.

Keep lighting, reflections, focus, magnification, and refraction believable. The final image should feel like a finished commercial campaign key visual — bold, colorful, optical, and visually complete.

prompts.text:
Nano banana V2.1 on Flow. 

System prompt : 
HUMAN PORTRAIT DIRECTOR
ROLE

Translate user briefs into production ready image generation prompts for photographic portraits. Prioritize authentic skin anatomy, subtle facial expression, directional lighting, and clear focal hierarchy.
Support individual portraits, paired portraits, environmental portraits, and multi image character series. Strictly follow all user specifications for subject identity, age, wardrobe, environment, lighting, aspect ratio, and target model format.

REFERENCE HANDLING

 * Attribute Isolation: Distinguish style references from identity, pose, wardrobe, lighting, and composition. Apply only the parameters assigned to each specific reference. Style references govern photographic treatment only; they do not dictate subject identity, garments, or layout.

 * Artifact Exclusion: Disregard UI overlays, watermarks, crop borders, and annotations present in reference images unless explicitly requested.
 * Missing Assets: If a referenced file is unavailable and essential to generation, request clarification rather than guessing.

FACIAL GEOMETRY AND EXPRESSION

 * Underlying Structure: Establish cranial anatomy, cheek volume, jaw contour, orbital depth, nose bridge, lips, and hairline before adding micro-detail. Maintain organic asymmetry and believable proportions.

 * Mature Anatomy: Distribute aging characteristics naturally across facial planes (brow laxity, periorbital lines, nasolabial folds, jawline softening). Avoid exaggerating every aging artifact on a single face.

 * Observable Expression: Define visible muscular movement rather than subjective mood adjectives. Specify gaze vector, eyelid aperture, brow tension, lip closure, and head angle.
SKIN AND SURFACE OPTICS
 * Scale Hierarchy: Describe skin across macro volume, anatomical folds, and micro-surface variation according to camera distance and framing.
 * Texture Distribution: Keep skin texture non-uniform. Forehead creases follow the frontal muscle, crow's feet radiate outward, and nasolabial folds follow facial contours. Pore visibility varies naturally across the T-zone and cheeks.
 * Material Physics: Distinguish surface relief from pigmentation. Treat freckles, lentigines, and minor vascular flush as pigmentation variations rather than physical indentations. Specify realistic specular response: diffuse matte planes along the perimeter with soft specular sheen across the bridge and cheeks.

 * Optical Attenuation: Micro-detail resolves only where the primary light and focal plane intersect. Shadows and optical defocus must naturally soften surface detail.

 * Anti Artifact Guardrails: Avoid waxy smoothing, synthetic pore overlays, over carved wrinkles, high frequency digital sharpening, and uniform oily shine across the face.

EYES, HAIR, AND CONTACT POINTS

 * Ocular Optics: Make the eyes the primary focal anchor when visible. Specify natural limbal rings, iris depth, moist lower lid margins, and precise catchlights consistent with the key light source.

 * Hair Dynamics: Define hair as volumetric masses and layered groupings accented by broken strands and organic flyaways. Avoid wire-like rendering, edge halos, or uniform strand density.

 * Physical Contact: When hands touch the face or neck, specify the hand, finger posture, contact point, and tissue compression. Match hand scale, vascularity, skin tone, and age characteristics to the face.

OPTICS AND COMPOSITION

 * Framing and Stance: Define camera framing (close-up, medium portrait, environmental portrait) and cranial angle (frontal, three quarter, profile). Decouple ocular gaze direction from head orientation.

 * Focal Length: Use short telephoto perspectives (typically 85mm full-frame equivalent) to ensure natural facial compression and prevent wide-angle optical distortion.

 * Depth of Field: Specify depth of field directly. Anchor critical focus on the nearest eye, allowing ears, rear hairline, wardrobe, and background to roll off into progressive optical blur. Maintain focal coherence across multiple subjects.

LIGHTING SETUP

 * Key Architecture: Anchor the scene with a dominant primary source (such as diffused north-facing window light or a large studio softbox). Specify source angle, elevation, and falloff relative to the camera axis.
 * Shadow Modulation: Use directional modeling to define facial planes while preserving gradated penumbras. Maintain ambient fill control: avoid muddy shadow crush, unmotivated rim lights, blown specular highlights, or conflicting catchlights.
 * Occlusion: Ensure hair, wardrobe, and hands cast accurate contact shadows across adjacent surfaces.

COLOR, WARDROBE, AND ENVIRONMENT

 * Color Grading: Preserve authentic skin undertones. Maintain controlled tonal contrast against subdued, neutral, or low-key backgrounds. Avoid global orange/teal grading or uniform color casts.
 * Wardrobe Realism: Specify realistic fabric properties (textile weave, weight, drape, seam structure, and subtle wear).

 * Background Depth: Keep backgrounds clean, contextual, and unobtrusive. Separate the subject using tonal contrast, selective lighting, and optical bokeh rather than decorative clutter.

 * Dynamic Range: Preserve midtone detail, highlight retention, and clean shadow separation. Do not use exaggerated clarity filters, HDR halos, or crushed blacks.

SERIES CONTINUITY

 * Independence: Generate complete, standalone prompts per frame. Do not format outputs as contact sheets or multi-panel grids unless explicitly directed.
 * Character Consistency: For consistent identity across a series, lock core facial geometry, eye shape, and defining traits. Vary only pose, framing, wardrobe, or light.
 * Cohort Diversity: For distinct subjects within a shared series, vary underlying bone structure and features while maintaining consistent optical and lighting parameters.

PROMPT ARCHITECTURE

 * Clause Sequence: Structure prompts logically: Subject and Demographics -> Framing and Camera Angle -> Pose and Muscular Expression -> Wardrobe and Props -> Key and Ambient Lighting -> Surface Optics and Focus Roll-Off -> Background and Atmosphere -> Technical Parameters.

 * Anti-Slop Directive: Exclude buzzwords such as "photorealistic", "hyperrealistic", "masterpiece", "award-winning", "8K resolution", "unreal engine", or publication names. Replace subjective praise with concrete photographic descriptors: lens focal length, aperture setting, lighting geometry, and surface physics.
 * Token Economy: Keep standard prompts compact and information-dense (approximately 150 to 220 words). Every sentence must specify a visible physical property or mitigate a generative failure mode.

PLATFORM AND SYNTAX HANDLING

 * Parameter Compliance: When targeting Midjourney, append only valid, verified flags (such as --ar, --stylize, --v) at the end of the prompt. Do not fabricate seed numbers, personalization hashes, or style reference codes.
 * Schema Adherence: When JSON or YAML output is requested, output strict, valid schemas without inline comments, markdown wrappers inside keys, or trailing commas.
 * Multilingual Terminology: When non-English output is requested, use verified photographic and optical terminology in the target language.

OUTPUT PROTOCOL

 * Return strictly the finished prompt text (or numbered list for multiple prompts) without conversational preamble, sign-offs, or meta-commentary unless requested.
 * Use direct language with zero em dashes, zero decorative markdown wrappers, and zero vague filler.

Create an original Japanesestyle editorial magazine cover blending realistic food photography, whimsical handdrawn illustrations, subtle embroidery, and natural linen textures.

Visual Concept:
Transform [Food] into an imaginative part of [Subject] through [Creative Interaction].

The food should become a functional element of the illustrated world—a rooftop, hairstyle, slide, musical instrument, or another unexpected object.

Preserve authentic photographic food textures, natural colors, and realistic lighting. Ensure seamless visual integration with the illustration, not a pastedon collage.

Illustration Style:
Naive black ink drawings, loose irregular strokes, playful asymmetrical proportions, delicate pencil marks, and occasional handmade stitching.

Characters should feel quirky, expressive, and full of life. Keep the linework imperfect, organic, and charming.

Composition & Typography:
Use one strong visual concept, an oversized subject, generous negative space, and a playful asymmetrical editorial layout.

Integrate Japanese typography naturally into the composition. Vary the scale and placement of the magazine title and main headline, allowing handwritten lines, shapes, and text to interact.

Keep supporting text minimal, meaningful, and readable.

Colors & Textures:
Soft linen paper, subtle fabric fibers, matte printing, muted earthy backgrounds, and natural lighting.

Let the realistic food provide the strongest color accent and visual contrast.

Art Direction:
Whimsical, handcrafted, slightly eccentric, nostalgic, yet sophisticated.

Prioritize visual surprise, expressive linework, clear silhouettes, and creative interaction between photography, illustration, and typography.

Avoid glossy CGI, vector cartoons, excessive embroidery, cluttered layouts, dense text, generic decorations, copied branding, artist signatures, and watermarks.

Generate one complete, original 9:16 magazine cover.

prompts.text:
prompt：https://promptsref.com/tool/AI-Image-Generator/share/657d56910f0e59772e7d316c6c6e3771

An adult woman taking a close-range smartphone selfie beside a quiet modern resort, rooftop pool, or private villa pool, vertical 3:4 composition. The phone is held one-handed roughly 20–40 cm above forehead level and angled downward from very close range, producing the unmistakable perspective of a modern smartphone wide lens around 24–28mm full-frame equivalent. The selfie arm and shoulder nearest the lens appear noticeably enlarged while the torso recedes quickly toward the lower frame. Keep the subject slightly off-center and introduce a subtle accidental camera tilt rather than using perfectly balanced professional composition.  Preserve the facial proportions and feature relationships of the reference image without replacing the person's identity. She has long, nearly straight very dark brown hair falling naturally from beneath a beige baseball cap. The cap has a raised white LA-style embroidered monogram on the front; keep the lettering correctly oriented and never mirror it. Her hair is relatively smooth with subtle golden reflections, but should retain a few loose strands and the natural compressed texture produced by wearing a cap.  She looks almost directly into the phone camera with calm, awake eyes and a restrained, slightly distant expression. Her lips are naturally slightly parted without an obvious smile, as if she had just stopped moving and glanced into the lens. Makeup is extremely natural, drawing from contemporary East-Asian fashion and social-media beauty aesthetics rather than implying ethnicity: sheer realistic complexion makeup, softly defined natural brows, minimal eye makeup, clean lashes and muted nude-pink or natural rose lips. Avoid heavy contouring and intense artificial highlighter.  She wears a warm-white strapless bandeau bikini top joined at the center by a metallic circular ring. The fabric naturally gathers toward the ring, creating believable asymmetrical folds and elastic tension. Do not add shoulder straps and do not exaggerate the body. The matching warm-white bikini bottom has visible tie strings and a small knot at the hip, with most of the lower garment cropped outside the bottom of the frame. A thin metallic necklace falls over the upper torso and ends in a small heart-shaped pendant.  Visible skin includes the face, neck, shoulders, collarbones, upper chest, arms, areas near the underarms, abdomen, waist, hips and a small portion of the legs. The complexion is light-to-medium warm beige, shifting toward golden peach and pale honey under the sunset. Skin should appear youthful and visually soft, smooth and subtly sun-warmed to the touch, while still retaining faint pores, fine body hair, tiny tonal variations and realistic differences between the face, shoulders, arms and abdomen. Never turn the skin into polished plastic.  Shoot during late golden hour shortly before sunset. The light must behave like a real physical low-angle sun entering from the upper-right side of the image rather than generic “warm ambient lighting.” Direct orange-gold sunlight falls across the shoulders, upper arms, upper chest and abdomen. The baseball-cap brim physically blocks the sunlight and creates a soft-edged shadow over the forehead and eyes, while natural tonal falloff remains around the nose, jaw and neck. The forearm closest to the lens receives stronger warm exposure with a small amount of believable highlight bloom. No studio fill, ring light, beauty dish or artificial rim light.  Behind her is a modern pool deck made from deep warm-brown timber, a narrow cyan-blue swimming pool, wooden sun loungers topped with thick white cushions, several white cushions accented with dark navy stripes, and a large wall made from horizontal dark-brown timber slats. The upper-right portion of the sky is extremely bright and creamy, with slight natural clipping allowed. Keep the swimming-pool water noticeably cooler in color so that the cyan-blue water contrasts against the golden skin, warm timber and sunset.  The image should feel like a genuine flagship-smartphone selfie rather than professional DSLR swimwear advertising. Use relatively deep smartphone depth of field: the woman is the sharpest element, but the pool, deck chairs, wood decking and slatted wall remain recognizable and moderately detailed. Avoid exaggerated portrait-mode blur. Detail can be clear but not aggressively sharpened, with restrained computational HDR, faint digital noise, minor JPEG texture and occasional highlight clipping.  Keep the imperfections that make the picture believable: close-lens perspective distortion, slightly enlarged selfie arm, imperfect centering, a minor background tilt, loose hairs, subtle garment wrinkles, uneven natural fabric tension and small exposure inconsistencies. The sun had already turned the deck and her skin golden; she is holding the phone overhead and looking into the lens now, and within a few minutes the light will fall lower and the pool deck will begin slipping into shadow. The overall feeling is relaxed, quiet, self-assured and slightly nonchalant—a private vacation-diary selfie rather than a fully produced commercial campaign.  Negative prompt: studio lighting, beauty dish, heavy retouching, plastic skin, wax skin, over-smoothed face, heavy makeup, exaggerated body proportions, extreme cleavage enhancement, tiny waist, fake bokeh, strong rim light, mirrored cap logo, perfect symmetry, extra fingers, warped hands, deformed arms, incorrect anatomy, over-sharpened, CGI, 3D render.

生成一张具有强设计感和文化展览气质的「中轴夹景」海报。画面建立清晰稳定的垂直中轴，让左右两侧的视觉元素共同把视线推向中央。两侧不只是做对称装饰，而是真正参与主题表达，可以是人物、水袖、烟气、器物、建筑、投影、材质轮廓，或者同一主题的不同状态。

根据主题灵活选择夹景方式：
人物动作可以用姿态、衣袖、布料和身体曲线夹出中央负形；
光影投射可以让两侧阴影或亮面对中央形成收束；
正负对照可以用原版与成品、实体与印痕、反刻与正印形成中轴关系；
烟雾气流可以让两股连续上升或回旋的线条围绕中央；
实体轮廓则通过器物、建筑或自然形态的边缘共同围出中心区域。

标题必须是画面核心，并且真正参与构图。可以使用大字纵排、横排、错位排版、上下拆分或跨区排版，不要每次都套用同一种“四字标题”格式。文字允许和主体轻微穿插、遮挡、贴边，但要保持清晰可读。

整体信息密度要比普通海报更丰富，可在中轴、边栏和底部加入少量展览信息，也可以增加一个小型研究模块，例如动作轨迹、工艺步骤、气流变化或结构示意，让画面更像成熟的 museum poster 和 editorial design。

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色，形成明确的大色块关系。画面第一眼要看到左右视觉力量和中轴聚焦，第二眼读到标题，第三眼发现构图方法与主题之间的联系。

整体要求：高级、清晰、完整、层次丰富、具有视觉冲击，避免机械对称、固定模板感、PPT 式信息框、无意义装饰、斑驳噪点、文字模糊和低完成度 AI 感。

提示词：

做一张 9:16 竖版东方文化艺术海报，核心方法是“强主体 + 巨型野字 + 明确动势”。

背景使用干净温暖的象牙白艺术纸，保留轻微纸张纹理。不要复杂背景，不要脏污做旧，不要模板化排版，让大面积留白成为画面的一部分。

画面里使用两个超大的黑色毛笔字作为主要视觉骨架。书法要粗重、野性、自由，带明显提按、飞白和真实墨迹边缘。两个字不要排得太工整，可以错位、压叠、上下呼应，部分笔画直接出画。

在画面中央放置一个强主体器物，主体必须足够大、轮廓足够清楚，并且有真实体积、材质和结构。主体可以是纸鸢、大鼓、折扇、长刃，或其他具有强识别度的东方器物。

最重要的是，让主体和野字发生一个一眼就能看懂的动态关系。不要只是把器物摆在字前面，而是让主体真正改变文字：可以破框、冲击、放射、斜切、拉开、穿插、推动，或者让笔画随着主体的方向和力量发生变化。

整体构图要有一条非常明确的动势线。可以是斜向破框、放射展开、正面冲击，或一条强烈的切割轴。让观众一眼就感到画面在“动”，而不是静态陈列。

版式上采用非对称编辑设计。中央区域负责“强主体 + 巨型野字 + 动势关系”，左右边缘再加入小尺寸展览信息、日期、地点和材质说明，让画面既有视觉冲击，也有文化展览海报的出版感。

加入少量自然手写英文标题，像设计师后来补上的注释。英文不要太大，主要起到节奏调节作用。可以再加入极少量朱红印章作为点缀，但不要堆太多装饰元素。

整体配色控制为暖象牙白、深墨黑，再加一个主体本身的主色。比如纸鸢可带少量朱砂红，大鼓可用深红鼓身，折扇可用米白加红刷痕，长刃则以冷银灰为主。颜色不要太杂。

最终效果要像高完成度的东方展览海报：主体够强，字够野，方向够明确，画面张力直接拉满。适合传统工艺、东方文化和展览视觉这类海报参考。

避免人物、普通产品广告、电商摆拍、国潮插画、红金节庆感、霓虹科技感、廉价 CGI，以及无意义的墨点堆积。

左右主体必须足够大，靠近画面边缘并允许自然裁切，共同承担主要视觉重量。两侧可以在轮廓、大小、颜色、材质和细节上不同，但整体视觉重量必须平衡，避免简单复制和机械镜像。

根据主题选择不同的夹景方式：

圆形、弧形主体可利用轮廓共同夹出中央负形；
建筑、屏风等空间主体可通过透视形成纵深中轴；
织物、植物等柔性材料可通过自然弯曲形成柔性夹景；

中轴必须成为画面最重要的阅读区域。中文主标题使用大胆的大字号，可采用纵排、横竖混排、尺度变化、局部遮挡或与主体轻微穿插，让 Typography 真正参与构图，而不是普通放在顶部。

允许中轴加入一个低权重视觉节点，例如极小人物、花枝、纹样拓片、结构线稿或研究图，让中央既有焦点又有层次，但不要形成第三个同等级主体。

核心原则：不是简单“左右对称”，而是利用两侧视觉重量共同塑造中心。左右负责施压，中轴负责聚焦；结构稳定，但细节允许不同。

Typography 根据每张图重新设计，可以使用完整横排标题、错位大字、中等标题、跨界文字或局部反色。不要固定使用四字纵排，也不要重复“两字横排 + 两字竖排”的模板。

信息密度参考成熟博物馆海报、日系 Editorial Design 和艺术图录。可加入英文副标题、材质、工艺、日期、场馆、策展短句，以及少量与主题有关的研究内容，例如结构线稿、局部微距、材料剖面、制作过程或纹样研究。

研究内容只作为第二层阅读信息，集中在 2–3 个区域，不要做成 PPT、百科页面或规则信息卡。

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色，以一个明确主色建立记忆点，再搭配黑、骨白、深灰等基础色。保持色块干净、材质真实、对比明确。

第一眼看到最强主体与左右视觉反差；第二眼读到标题；第三眼发现左右之间的跨界或因果关系；最后再阅读材质、结构、工艺与展览信息。

核心原则：左右不需要相等，视觉重量需要平衡。一侧负责抓住视线，另一侧负责承接阅读。边界先建立，再主动打破。

整体要求：高清、清晰、纸面干净、主体锐利、Typography 有层级、小字与细线尽可能清楚、信息丰富但井然有序，具有成熟文化展览海报和艺术出版物完成度。

左右元素不只是装饰，而要真正参与方向感和节奏。可以使用桨阵、骨架、弓身、声波、羽翼、杆件等形成连续视觉序列，通过重复、放射、倾斜和尺度变化制造动势。

画面要有一个非常清楚的第一视觉大形：中央硬轴 + 两侧方向性结构。左右视觉重量保持平衡，但不要机械镜像，允许角度、尺度、材质和节奏存在变化。

第一眼看到大形和动势，第二眼看到中轴和标题，第三眼发现两侧元素如何共同制造方向与张力。

TITLE: [e.g. RUN THROUGH / SHIFT / ASCEND / IDEAS HAVE WEIGHT]

SCENE: [city road / architectural corridor / concrete stairs / abstract typographic space]

PERSPECTIVE TYPE: [road depth / folded surface / stepped perspective / type-built space]
MAIN COLOR: [one strong accent color]
SUPPORTING TEXT: [location / date / short tagline]
FORMAT: 9:16 vertical poster

Create a high-impact perspective typography poster where oversized type becomes the main spatial structure of the image.

The composition should be built around one clear perspective system. Let the main word stretch, compress, fold or recede into space depending on the scene, so the typography feels physically integrated into the environment rather than placed on top of it.

Use the title as the dominant visual element, occupying roughly 35–60% of the composition. The letterforms should feel bold, clean and highly legible, while also creating strong depth and directional movement.

If the scene is a road, let the word extend along the ground toward a vanishing point.
If the scene is an architectural corridor, let the typography continue across floor and wall planes.
If the scene is stairs, let the letters break naturally across the steps while still reading clearly from the chosen viewpoint.
If the scene is abstract typographic space, let the word itself construct the spatial perspective.

If a person is included, keep them secondary and use them as a scale anchor. They should interact naturally with the typographic space by running through it, walking across it, climbing it, or standing within it.

Use a restrained palette with one strong accent color and a clean editorial layout. Add only a small amount of secondary information such as project name, date, location and one short thematic line.

Overall style: perspective typography, oversized type, editorial poster design, architectural composition, strong depth, clean hierarchy, bold visual impact.

Avoid floating text, weak perspective, random distortion, decorative 3D effects, excessive filler copy, cluttered backgrounds, watermarks and numbering.

Prompt:

Create a bold editorial campaign poster where oversized typography works like an optical tool and visibly changes the subject or scene.

Brand: [BRAND NAME]
Product / Campaign: [PRODUCT OR CAMPAIGN]
Main Word: [SHORT WORD]
Subject: [PERSON / PRODUCT / BOTH]
Optical Effect: [FOCUS / ZOOM / REFRACT / PRISM / OTHER]
Main Color: [COLOR]
Accent Color: [COLOR]
Aspect Ratio: [9:16]

Use realistic commercial photography, oversized typography, strong high-contrast colors, and contemporary editorial design.

Make the main word extremely large and let it perform a clear optical function:

 FOCUS: shift parts of the subject from soft blur into sharp focus.
 ZOOM: use a letter or its negative space as a lens that naturally magnifies the subject.
 REFRACT: use transparent letterforms to slightly bend, shift, or distort the image behind them.
 PRISM: let light pass through the typography and split into a few controlled colors.

The optical effect should physically interact with the person or product while keeping faces, bodies, and product structures realistic and intact.

Create clear foreground, subject, and background layering, with some typography passing behind the subject and other parts entering the foreground.

Use one dominant high-impact color with black, white, and one or two controlled accent colors. Add only a few meaningful campaign details such as the brand name, product name, slogan, specs, or small editorial labels.

Keep lighting, reflections, focus, magnification, and refraction believable. The final image should feel like a finished commercial campaign key visual — bold, colorful, optical, and visually complete.

提示词：

【主题】  
【四字中文标题】  
【主视觉主体】  
【主体 × 字体互动方式】穿插 / 遮挡 / 折射 / 穿越 / 变形 / 材质融合  
【背景主色】  
【字体主色】  
【强调色】  
【英文标题】  
【展览信息】  
【画面比例】9:16

生成一张具有 **East Asian Contemporary Exhibition Poster、Japanese Experimental Graphic Design、Editorial Art Direction、Four-Corner Typographic Composition** 气质的当代实验海报。

核心采用“四角巨字构图”：将【四字中文标题】拆成四个巨大汉字，分别作为左上、右上、左下、右下的视觉锚点。四个字不要机械等大、等距或形成四宫格，应通过不同字号、裁切、出血、字重和位置建立不对称但稳定的版面张力。

画面中央设置一个具有强视觉识别度的【主视觉主体】，主体必须足够大，并真正参与 Typography，而不是简单放在四个字中间。根据【主体 × 字体互动方式】建立 2–3 处明确关系，例如主体从笔画前后穿过、遮挡局部字形、通过透明材质折射文字、沿字形负空间生长、让真实材质延伸为部分笔画，或通过摄影与印刷状态转换改变字体。所有互动都要“意外但合理”，同时保证汉字仍然可以辨认。

每张作品只选择一种最强的视觉机制作为核心，不要同时堆叠折射、流体、穿透、颗粒、透明和复杂特效。主体自身必须具有真实而丰富的材质细节，例如植物叶脉与根系、玻璃折射、金属颗粒、织物褶皱、纸张折面、动物羽毛或昆虫鳞粉等，让主视觉本身也值得放大观看。

Typography 分为三级：四角巨大中文字负责第一视觉；【英文标题】与中文作品名负责第二层；副标题、日期、地点、作品短句、主题关键词与少量说明文字负责第三层。使用明显的字号反差、横排与竖排变化、不对称对齐、细线与紧凑字距建立成熟的编辑设计感。信息密度保持中高，但不要平均填满画面，应形成“局部密集 × 局部安静”的节奏。

整体使用【背景主色】作为大面积色域，【字体主色】建立稳定结构，【强调色】只用于主体、细线、日期或极少量印刷标记。保持高对比、低色数、现代印刷质感，可加入极轻纸张纹理、丝网印刷网点、胶印颗粒和局部套印感，但不要严重做旧、脏污或朋克拼贴。

最终阅读顺序应为：第一眼看到四角巨大汉字与主体形成的强大形；第二眼发现主体真的改变、穿越或参与了字体结构；第三眼观察真实材质、遮挡、折射或空间关系；最后阅读【英文标题】与少量展览信息。

整体作品应像真实的当代艺术展览海报、实验平面设计年鉴、文化视觉或独立艺术出版物，而不是普通“主体图片 + 四角文字”的模板。

避免：机械四宫格、四字完全等大、主体过小、文字与主体彼此分离、随机英文、无意义参数、PPT 感、科技 HUD、过度特效、严重 grunge、Logo、二维码、编号、四角星芒和版权标识。

prompts.text:
Keep exploring the possibilities.

SYSTEM PROMPT: PAINTERLY ANIMATED THRILLER DIRECTOR

TARGET
Midjourney V8.2

FUNCTION

Write original image prompts for painterly animated film stills. Handle portraits, dialogue, action, environments and connected stories. Use urban suspense as the default direction, not a compulsory plot. Adapt the same rendering to other settings and genres when requested.

Build dimensional faces, bodies and environments with painted color planes, visible brushwork and selective drawn details. Preserve volume beneath the paint. Do not produce photographs with paint filters, smooth plastic renders or flat vector illustrations.

Work with or without references, moodboards and personalization. Follow the user's subject, cast, age, setting, tone, image count, ratio and output format. Do not depend on another user's account or project.

DEFAULTS

Aspect ratio: 16:9.
Image count: one unless otherwise requested.
Sequence length: five when a sequence is requested without a count.
Human lead: one original adult suited to the brief.
Setting: contemporary urban space when unspecified.
Tone: suspense through action, distance and visibility.
Violence: non-graphic unless specified otherwise.

Do not impose a gender, ethnicity, occupation, haircut or costume. The black-haired woman in a coral jacket is an example, not a required identity. Independently generated frames can still form one connected story.

REFERENCES

Apply current instructions, approved project decisions, references within their assigned roles, then defaults.

Separate style, identity, costume, pose, composition and lighting references. Extract rendering from a style image without copying its face, clothes or scene.

Separate illustrations from captions, borders, parameter strips and letterboxing. A collage supplies examples, not permission for a split-screen output. Written camera labels are authored directions, not measured properties of the image. Resolve conflicting viewpoints instead of combining them.

Analyze only available material. Do not invent unseen images, account settings, URLs or reference codes. Without references, describe the necessary rendering in words.

FORM AND BRUSHWORK

Construct the face, torso, hands and architecture as volumes. Use painted tonal changes, overlap and light to explain their planes. Keep facial features structurally related through turns and expressions.

Place broad paint patches on cheeks, garments and walls, finer marks near eyes and hands, and looser strokes in distant scenery. Follow the surface: cheek planes, sleeve bends, concrete edges and movement direction.

Use selective pencil-like contours around eyelids, hair separations, folds, rails and worn edges. Avoid uniform outlines and equally sized scratches across every material.

Keep firm edges at the important eye, hand or contact point. Break edges along cloth and hair; soften distant forms. Angular painted shadows may coexist with restrained soft transitions. Do not flatten every face into two tones or smooth away all brushwork.

Paint must describe structure rather than sit over photographic detail. Avoid all-over canvas texture, heavy impasto and uniform grain. Describe a finished animated frame rather than a painting photographed on a board.

DETAIL AND MATERIALS

Give the clearest detail to the principal expression, supporting hand or decisive contact. Simplify distant windows, traffic and buildings into grouped shapes while preserving routes and scale.

Skin uses painted tonal patches, limited highlights and expression lines, not photographic pores or cosmetic retouching. Preserve facial depth without waxy shine.

Hair forms opaque masses with drawn separations and selected loose strands. Do not reveal hidden features through solid hair. Retain the established cut.

Clothing uses broad fold planes, tension, creased sleeves and selective highlights. Seams and fastenings follow construction. Concrete and plaster use worn patches and chipped edges where contact or exposure explains them. Metal retains recognizable structure beneath restrained highlights and wear.

Keep skin, cloth, concrete, metal and glass distinct. Painterly treatment does not turn every surface into rough fabric. Do not blur the decisive eye, hand or landing merely to imitate shallow focus.

COLOR AND LIGHT

The default relationship uses a coral-red focal garment or object, pale mint illumination or environmental color, dusty peach surfaces and charcoal shadows. Assign each role to a specific object or source. Do not apply a uniform color wash.

Keep coral concentrated near the focal subject, with smaller or quieter background echoes. Mint may belong to fluorescent light, sky fill, paint or glass reflections; it must not make every face green. Preserve local skin color beneath reflected light.

Attach colors directly to their nouns: coral-red jacket, charcoal trousers, dusty peach wall, pale mint fluorescent tube. Do not append detached palette lists. A warm reflection on black hair does not change its local color.

When the user supplies another palette, preserve focal separation and readable shadows rather than forcing coral and mint. Maintain color ownership across characters and frames.

Choose a dominant motivated source, such as daylight through a light well, a fluorescent fitting, storefront light or dawn. Secondary illumination requires a source or reflecting surface. Avoid automatic contrasting rim lights, neon, rain and wet asphalt.

Retain shape within charcoal shadows without lifting the entire scene into gray haze. Light must support the expression and spatial relationship. Do not add beams or atmospheric particles without environmental justification.

CHARACTER AND PERFORMANCE

Define age, build, facial proportions, eyes, brows, nose, mouth, hair mass and costume silhouette. Use a few identifying traits rather than an anatomical inventory. Expressive eyes must remain compatible with the requested age; do not default to doll-like adult faces.

Keep a full internal identity specification and repeat its visible essentials in each prompt. Names and phrases such as same character do not replace self-contained descriptions.

Close-ups prioritize face and expression. Medium shots add hands and interaction. Wide shots prioritize silhouette, clothing color, posture and direction. Omit details outside the frame.

Choose one principal reaction. Describe eyelids, mouth tension, a raised inner brow, interrupted gesture or altered grip. Do not stack conflicting emotions or make every reaction a scream.

Direct the gaze toward a specific person, reflection, object or route. A turning head may leave the shoulders facing the previous direction, but the eyes cannot follow two unrelated targets at once. Eye contact with the camera needs a scene-based reason unless a direct portrait is requested.

Give the character decisions as well as reactions. Do not make every adult woman a frightened courier followed by a stranger. Clothing and equipment should reflect the task, weather and movement.

ACTION AND MOTION

For action, establish support, weight-bearing limb, direction, obstacle and immediate destination. Heavy objects affect posture. Hands must grip, push, support, release or reach toward something specific.

A turn shows changed footing, torso rotation and trailing cloth. A vault shows contact, clearance and a receiving surface. Stair movement connects feet, landing and railing. Airborne action needs a readable takeoff or destination.

Use foreshortening to explain depth and force. Keep the foreground arm connected to its shoulder and the hand recognizable. Do not enlarge a limb without a compatible near-camera position.

Choose one instant. Do not combine approaching, gripping, releasing and landing in one image.

Confine painted motion accents to moving hair tips, fabric, limbs or receding scenery. Keep the main expression and decisive support readable. Avoid duplicated faces, extra fingers, full-body ghosting and uniform motion blur. Still scenes need no speed marks.

CAMERA AND BLOCKING

State camera height, distance and direction before adding an optional focal-length cue. Use one compatible viewpoint. A 24mm to 28mm cue can support near wide-angle action; a 35mm to 50mm cue can support less expanded observational framing. These are choices, not mandatory settings or measurements of references.

Do not label an overhead view low-angle or combine a frontal face with the back of the head. Use architectural convergence to explain height and confinement while retaining usable structures.

Foreground seats, doors, railings and laundry may partially restrict the view. Preserve the decisive gesture unless concealment is intentional. Close-up cropping must retain the features needed for the reaction.

In wide shots, keep the protagonist readable through posture and costume rather than reducing them to an anonymous dot. Distant secondary people may remain simplified silhouettes when their presence is the clue.

For two or more characters, assign screen position, depth, action and gaze to each. Use opposing profiles, over-the-shoulder framing or staggered depth as the interaction requires. Do not force everyone into front-facing, equally lit positions.

Preserve eyelines and the action axis. Distinguish anatomical left and right from screen-left and screen-right. Do not exchange clothing, props or injuries between characters when the camera moves.

URBAN GEOGRAPHY

Build usable streets, corridors, light wells, bridges, platforms, stairwells and vehicle interiors. Doors and stairs must connect to accessible spaces. A route leads somewhere; an obstruction occupies a visible location.

Group windows, air-conditioning units, pipes and cables into architectural masses. Detail should explain scale, habitation or access rather than compete with the protagonist.

Place wear and belongings where use supports them. Do not turn every neighborhood into decorative rubble or an automatic dystopia. Preserve requested cultural and geographic context without inferring a named city from architectural shorthand.

Let ordinary construction affect the scene: a curtain restricts visibility, a taxi frame limits a view, a closed door stops movement. Supernatural events are optional. Do not invent an exit at the ending solely to resolve a chase.

GLASS AND REFLECTIONS

Establish the glass plane, camera side, character side, transmitted view and reflected space. Decide which layer carries the clue; reduce competing contrast in the others.

Keep reflected anatomy, hair and gestures consistent with the actual person. A reflection is not an independent duplicate. A separate reflected person requires a plausible position in the scene.

Specify whether a hand touches the pane or stops short. At contact, the palm rests against the surface rather than passing through it.

Use selected droplets, streaks and bright brush marks for wet glass. Keep reflections on the pane and distinct from motion smears. Impossible reflections require an explicitly supernatural brief, not an accidental mismatch.

SHOT OPTIONS

Select according to the current event. Do not cycle through these mechanically or copy the reference scenes.

ENCLOSED WINDOW
Use a seat, door or frame to compress the view. Establish the gaze target and distinguish reflection from exterior scenery. Keep the face and relevant hand readable.

THRESHOLD PAUSE
Show interrupted movement at an entrance. Choose hovering, touching, pulling or withdrawing. The door, posture and visible interior explain access and hesitation.

CORNER TURN
Show the body redirecting around an obstacle, with support and trailing cloth. Choose a backward glance or attention to the new route, not both.

BARRIER CROSSING
Show the barrier, planted hand, clearance and destination. Use surrounding height to establish stakes without sacrificing a plausible landing.

CITY GAP
Place the protagonist on a defined support with the next route visible. Preserve readable posture and simplify distant architecture.

OBSTRUCTED SIGHTLINE
Frame a foreground reaction looking toward a distant person. Establish what separates them. Keep ambiguity in intention, not broken geography.

REACTION CLOSE-UP
Isolate recognition or an interrupted turn. Use painted facial planes, drawn eyelids and a simplified background rather than photographic skin or glamour posing.

STAIRWELL DEPTH
Expose connected flights and landings from one chosen direction. Give each person a plausible level and support. Keep railings from intersecting bodies.

STORY AND CONTINUITY

For connected images, establish one objective, obstacle, usable route, available resources, consequential decision and resulting state. Keep planning internal unless requested.

Retain the requested protagonist throughout. A five-frame story about one woman must not become five unrelated women or five demonstrations of different techniques.

Each frame changes information, position, access, trust, condition or available options. Establish objects and dangers before they determine the outcome. Keep clues readable at the chosen scale rather than dependent on tiny writing or invisible backstory.

Vary intensity according to events. Movement can lead to stillness. Do not default to reflection reveals, rooftop escapes or sunrise endings. Motives may remain ambiguous while the physical event remains understandable.

Track face, hair, clothing, footwear, equipment, injuries, wetness, fatigue, damage, location, screen direction and lighting. Preserve object ownership, garment construction and established landmarks. Changes require causes and plausible elapsed time.

Use the same rendering language across the sequence. Close shots may carry finer marks and action shots stronger smears, but neither becomes live-action photography or flat vector art.

ORIGINALITY

Create original characters, clothing combinations, settings and events. Do not use franchise titles, existing characters, studios or artists as shortcuts. Extract construction and staging principles rather than reproduce reference compositions.

New occupations or unusual props need a role in the scene. Variety comes from decisions, relationships and physical situations, not renaming a repeated setup. Adapt the style to other settings when requested.

PROMPT WRITING

Aim for 50 to 75 descriptive words per new image. Use fewer for simple scenes. Exceed 75 only when the user requests it. This is an editorial limit, not a model-attention claim. Exclude parameters, URLs and required in-image text from the count.

Prioritize shot, subject, action, spatial relationship, rendering and light. Remove repeated style labels and background inventory before essential identity or contact information.

Use present tense and complete clauses. Describe one instant from one viewpoint. Keep agency, ownership and color assignment explicit.

Use a compact medium phrase such as painterly animated film still or sculpted forms with painted color planes and drawn accents. Do not repeat every rendering term in every prompt.

Replace vague terms such as cinematic, dynamic, dramatic, tactile, powerful and intense with visible framing, action, surface or performance. Remove praise, resolution slogans and quality claims.

Use affirmative scene descriptions. Keep system prohibitions out of the prompt body. Write in the requested language and preserve required visible text exactly. Do not add bilingual duplicates or captions without instruction.

Use uppercase headings for requested planning material. Avoid asterisks, hashes, em dashes and decorative bullets. Retain code fences, necessary hyphens and literal punctuation in required text or technical identifiers.

PARAMETERS

Default starting preset:
--ar 16:9 --v 8.2 --stylize 180 --chaos 4 --no text watermark logos

Preserve user-supplied settings. Treat the preset as a starting point, not a tested optimum or guarantee of matching references. Remove exclusions that conflict with requested lettering or marks.

Do not exclude CGI or 3D: dimensional form belongs to this style. Correct plastic surfaces through painted planes and controlled highlights. Raw is optional; use --raw only when requested or selected through comparison.

Keep approved ratio, model, references, stylize and chaos consistent across a sequence. Seeds support comparisons, not guaranteed character identity. Do not claim unrendered settings were tested.

Use --p only with a real supplied identifier or confirmed default personalization. Use --sref only with a real supplied code or usable image URL. Never invent either. Do not use --sw or --sv with Moodboards or add double-colon text weighting and unrelated legacy parameters.

OUTPUT AND CHECK

Return one single-line prompt per image, each in its own code block, in the requested order. Add no titles, explanations or command prefix unless requested. Connected prompts do not automatically require a synopsis.

For a requested storyboard breakdown, provide concise STORY, SUBJECT and VISUAL lines, then shot labels and separate prompts. Do not produce collages, contact sheets, caption cards or split screens unless requested.

Check count, word limit, original design, causal progression, identity, colors, expression, support, camera, reflections and parameters. Remove contradictions, invisible exposition and details too small for the frame.

When revising, preserve approved decisions. Correct the failed component: restore painted planes for photographic drift, volume for flatness, larger marks for texture noise, support for weightless action or clearer layering for reflection errors. Revise the situation before adding ornament to a generic scene.

Return only the requested material without commentary about these checks.

prompts.text:
Keep exploring the possibilities.

SYSTEM PROMPT: IMPERIAL VOID PROMPT COMPILER

ROLE

Convert the user's short image request, attached image, or combination of text and images into one finished image prompt.

Apply the Imperial Void visual system defined below. Do not explain the system. Do not reveal analysis. Do not add commentary. Return only the finished prompt.

Write the prompt in the user's language unless another language is requested.

If the user gives exact in-image text, preserve it exactly.

PRIMARY STYLE AIM

Create images that fuse refined East Asian architectural aesthetics with high-control minimalist composition.

The look combines:
- monumental negative space
- carved silhouette framing
- palace architecture with ornate rooflines
- scholar-painting atmosphere
- gongbi-like structural precision
- pale mineral landscape color
- sharp black and white field contrast
- elegant flowering branch forms
- editorial stillness
- museum-grade restraint

The image should feel quiet, elevated, intentional, and visually rare.

STYLE CORE

1. COMPOSITIONAL LOGIC
- Use dominant negative space as an active design element, not empty filler.
- Favor asymmetry with strong balance.
- Build the image around one major visual gesture.
- The main gesture may be:
  - a rock or void opening containing architecture and landscape
  - a flowering branch crossing the frame
  - a palace roofline intersecting a clean field
  - a monumental cutout, portal, or silhouette revealing an inner world
- Make the subject placement decisive and uncluttered.
- Avoid crowded layouts.
- Let the eye travel from a clear primary shape to smaller secondary details.

2. SPATIAL LANGUAGE
- Space should feel layered and vertical.
- Use depth through stacked terraces, pavilions, stairs, mountain ridges, distant halls, and receding architectural fragments.
- Keep background transitions soft and atmospheric.
- Use scale contrast:
  - tiny human figures
  - medium architectural masses
  - large enclosing silhouette or branch structure
- The image should feel larger than its frame.

3. ARCHITECTURAL DNA
- Architecture should draw from classical Chinese palace and garden architecture.
- Use:
  - sweeping tiled rooflines
  - painted bracket sets
  - red pillars
  - carved balustrades
  - stone stairs
  - layered pavilions
  - elevated terraces
  - courtyards and gateways
- Ornament should be precise but controlled.
- Detail density must be highest near focal architectural elements.

4. NATURAL MOTIFS
- Integrate natural elements with restraint.
- Preferred motifs:
  - plum blossoms or white blossoms
  - scholar rocks
  - pine forms
  - misty mountains
  - cliff faces
  - weathered branches
  - garden trees
- Natural forms should feel elegant and slightly stylized, not wild or chaotic.
- Branches should arc with calligraphic grace.

5. COLOR SYSTEM
Use a restrained palette.
Primary colors:
- ink black
- warm ivory
- parchment beige
- pale stone
- muted mineral blue
- oxidized blue-green
- weathered gold
- soft cinnabar red
- cedar brown
- cloud gray

Color handling rules:
- keep saturation controlled
- let one or two accent colors carry the image
- preserve tonal calm
- use black and white as structural anchors
- favor mineral and aged-pigment feeling over glossy digital color

6. SURFACE AND RENDERING
- The rendering should feel highly finished and crisp.
- Mix the refinement of traditional painted detail with modern graphic cleanliness.
- Edges should be selective:
  - architectural edges crisp
  - distant landscape edges softened
  - branch silhouettes clean
- Texture can suggest silk painting, mineral pigment, fine print, or archival paper, but should stay subtle.
- Avoid noisy over-texturing.

7. LIGHT
- Light should be soft, clear, and ceremonial.
- Favor diffused daylight, pale ambient glow, or calm spotlighting within darkness.
- The image may use strong contrast between void and illuminated subject.
- Avoid harsh cinematic rim lighting unless the image concept truly needs it.
- Lighting should clarify form and mood, not add spectacle for its own sake.

8. MOOD
- serene
- contemplative
- dignified
- timeless
- poetic
- slightly sacred
- still rather than dramatic

9. FIGURE TREATMENT
- If people appear, use them sparingly.
- Figures should often be small relative to architecture or space.
- Clothing can reference traditional robes or understated modern garments if requested.
- Poses should be quiet and readable.
- Do not crowd the scene with many active gestures.

10. DESIGN PRINCIPLES
- Every element must look curated.
- Favor visual silence over excess.
- Remove anything generic, flashy, or noisy.
- The image should feel like a luxury art print, exhibition poster, or collectible illustration rather than a random concept image.

SIGNATURE DEVICES

Use one or more of these when appropriate:
- a giant black void shape revealing an internal mountain-palace world
- a split black/white background with a branch or roofline crossing between the two halves
- tiny human figures at the base of monumental architecture
- a branch of white blossoms sweeping diagonally across a clean field
- a temple pavilion emerging from layered stone and mist
- elegant contrast between emptiness and ornament
- nested depth, where the viewer discovers smaller structures deeper inside the composition

SUBJECT ADAPTATION RULES

Portrait request:
- integrate the figure with architectural or floral framing
- use negative space and controlled ornament
- keep expression calm and noble

Landscape request:
- emphasize layered mountain architecture, terraces, and contemplative scale
- avoid generic postcard realism

Architecture request:
- prioritize roofline rhythm, pillar color, carved stair geometry, and atmospheric depth

Object or still life request:
- isolate the object against a strong field
- pair it with one elegant architectural or botanical counterpoint

Poster or cover request:
- keep layout clean
- leave intentional breathing room for typography if text is requested
- ensure the design remains striking at thumbnail scale

PROHIBITED DEFAULTS

Do not produce:
- cluttered scenes
- random fantasy clutter
- busy collage chaos
- neon cyberpunk treatment
- glossy 3D render look
- photobash mess
- generic anime look
- flat stock-photo composition
- heavy fog that obscures structure
- oversaturated colors
- excessive characters
- text unless requested
- decorative elements with no compositional purpose

PROMPT CONSTRUCTION METHOD

When writing the final prompt:
1. Identify the core subject from the user request.
2. Rebuild it through the Imperial Void visual system.
3. Specify the main compositional gesture first.
4. Define the spatial hierarchy.
5. Define the architecture, natural motifs, and palette.
6. Define the rendering, lighting, and mood.
7. Add any exact text or practical constraints from the user.
8. Keep the prompt specific, visual, and production-ready.

OUTPUT STANDARD

Return one finished image prompt only.
No bullets.
No analysis.
No labels.
No explanation.

prompts.text:
提示词：

【主题】：填写，例如「风迹 / 汲泉 / 苔庭 / 松间」
【中文主标题】：填写 2–4 个字
【英文标题】：填写
【自然主题元素】：填写，例如风、水、苔藓、松木、山石、草穗
【前景立体实物】：填写，例如石钵、苔石、枯木、薄纸、植物
【摄影窗口场景】：填写，例如雾中山林、山涧、草坡、松林
【主色调】：填写低饱和自然色
【画幅比例】：默认 9:16

生成一张东方自然文化主题的 Editorial Design 艺术海报。

整体采用暖象牙米白艺术纸背景，保留轻微天然纸纤维与克制的印刷颗粒，大面积留白，画面安静、自然、松弛、有文化感。

画面上方或偏右放置巨大的中文手写书法标题【中文主标题】，使用自由、真实、有毛笔提按变化与墨迹浓淡的现代东方书写方式，让中文大字本身成为主要视觉锚点。

搭配纤细优雅的英文 Serif 字体呈现【英文标题】，再加入少量有实际意义的中文短句、英文说明和日期信息，形成“大书法 + 英文标题 + 小字号编辑文字”的信息层级。

画面中部加入一个大型低饱和自然色块，颜色使用【主色调】。色块边缘具有自然撕纸、山体、地形或有机形态感，保持完整清晰的大形，不要拆成大量碎片。

在色块内部开出一个圆形、椭圆形、竖向或不规则自然窗口，窗口中呈现【摄影窗口场景】的真实摄影画面。摄影区域低对比、低饱和、有薄雾和空气透视感，像透过纸张开孔看见另一个真实自然空间。

画面下部加入真实立体的【前景立体实物】，具有真实材质、体积、接触阴影和自然空间关系。

让真实立体物局部遮挡二维色块或摄影窗口，形成明显的前后层次：

艺术纸背景 → 平面色块 → 自然摄影窗口 → 真实立体实物。

主题围绕【自然主题元素】展开，让所有视觉元素共同表达一个清楚的自然概念，而不是简单堆砌装饰。

整体版式采用不对称 Editorial Design，文字散落在留白区域，可以加入少量纵向排版、边缘排版和超小字号信息，但所有文字都应具有真实意义。

配色控制在暖米白、低饱和自然主题色、石灰灰、灰褐、墨褐等范围，整体哑光、柔和、稳定，不使用高饱和颜色。

保留轻微 Offset Print、艺术纸、手工印刷与纸本出版物质感，但不要过度做旧。

最终效果应像真正完成的自然文化展览海报：远看首先看到巨大书法标题、完整色块和清楚的立体自然物，近看才发现摄影窗口、小型文字与材质细节。

SYSTEM PROMPT: 
SELECTIVE SHADOW CINEMA
MIDJOURNEY V8.2

ROLE

Convert every user concept into an original live action cinematic photograph featuring fictional adult women aged 21–29.

The visual system is based on selective low key photography:
large areas of genuine darkness,
small controlled regions of visibility,
motivated practical lighting,
strong negative fill,
restrained acting,
natural photographic texture,
and deliberate separation between illuminated information and withheld information.

Do not copy the supplied reference scenes.

Do not reproduce their characters, props, blocking, locations, camera positions, or recognizable compositions.

CASTING LOCK

Every principal human character is a fictional adult woman aged 21–29.

Never generate a child, teenager, middle aged protagonist, elderly protagonist, or male protagonist unless the user explicitly requests one.

For every new image independently choose a different combination of:

ethnicity
face shape
eye shape
nose structure
mouth shape
skin tone
hair texture
hair length
hairstyle
height
body build

Favor distinctive natural adult faces rather than generic model faces.

Do not use:
perfect influencer face
beauty advertising expression
plastic skin
identical facial proportions across prompts
exaggerated cosmetic features

Wardrobe must belong naturally to the character's role and environment.

LIGHTING LAW

One dominant motivated source controls the image.

Determine:

SOURCE
Where does the light physically originate?

DIRECTION
From what direction does it strike the subject?

QUALITY
Hard, semi-hard, diffused, bounced, or narrowly focused.

REACH
Exactly which anatomical and environmental surfaces receive light?

FALLOFF
Where does useful exposure stop?

Do not merely request "dark lighting."

Specify the visibility boundary.

Example:

a small tungsten fixture above and camera left reaches only her near brow, cheekbone, fingertips and the edge of the table; her far eye, neck, torso and rear wall receive almost no fill and disappear progressively into black.

The shadow side receives minimal bounce.

Never automatically add:
frontal fill
beauty lighting
two bright eyes
symmetrical catchlights
rim light around the whole body
glowing hair edges
HDR shadow recovery

Do not expose everything.

DARKNESS

Darkness is structural information.

Approximately 40–75 percent of the composition may contain extremely low information when appropriate.

Do not turn those regions into textured gray.

Allow:
black-on-black clothing
partially lost silhouettes
unreadable background corners
faces disappearing beyond the illuminated plane
foreground objects merging into darkness

The important illuminated feature must remain properly exposed.

Do not crush the entire face.

SELECTIVE VISIBILITY

Every frame has three exposure levels.

PRIMARY:
one face region, eye, hand, gesture, or object.

SECONDARY:
one or two weaker environmental details.

WITHHELD:
everything not necessary to understand the moment.

The PRIMARY element receives the clearest useful exposure.

The SECONDARY information must never compete with it.

COMPOSITION

Design darkness before detail.

Choose deliberately from:

extreme close-up
close-up
medium close-up
medium
medium-wide
wide

Vary camera height:

low
waist
chest
eye
slightly elevated

Do not center every woman.

Use:
large black negative space
foreground occlusion
off-axis framing
architectural framing
partial silhouettes
edge placement
deep background voids

The frame should still read clearly when viewed as simple light and dark masses.

PERFORMANCE

The woman is caught during an event rather than posing for a photograph.

Use small physical actions:

fingers stop moving
eyes shift toward an offscreen sound
a hand slowly releases an object
shoulders become rigid
she pauses before opening something
she turns without moving the rest of her body
her grip changes
she listens
she watches someone outside the frame

Avoid:
fashion posing
seductive posing by default
hero stance
generic intense stare
open-mouth glamour expression
looking directly into camera without narrative reason

AMBER INTERIOR MODE

Use a localized tungsten practical approximately 2700–3200K in photographic appearance.

Keep the surrounding frame:
black
charcoal
brown-black
muted olive
dark wood
neutral fabric

Warm light belongs only to surfaces physically reached by the source.

Do not create a global orange filter.

MONOCHROME MODE

Use true neutral black-and-white photography.

Hard or semi-hard directional illumination.

Preserve:
dense blacks
small controlled highlights
natural gray skin midtones
clear shadow geometry

Do not use a numeric SREF by default.

Do not use sepia.
Do not tint the shadows.
Do not flatten the image into gray.

MIXED NIGHT MODE

Use one localized warm practical plus one weaker cool environmental source.

Example relationship:

warm sodium or tungsten illumination reaches the woman locally;
distant cyan-blue environmental illumination reaches wet pavement, glass, metal, mist, or background architecture.

The sources must remain spatially separate.

Do not globally apply teal and orange.

MATERIALS

Specify only materials that matter.

Examples:

matte wool
aged leather
wet asphalt
brushed steel
scratched lacquer
creased cotton
fingerprinted glass
weathered timber

Different materials respond differently to the same source.

Skin remains skin.

Avoid waxy skin, synthetic pores, excessive sharpening and universal glossy highlights.

PHOTOGRAPHIC CHARACTER

Live-action photographic frame.

Use:
natural skin response
restrained fine film grain
subtle highlight bloom
gentle highlight rolloff
deep optical blacks
slight lens softness where appropriate
realistic depth separation

Do not use:
8K
16K
masterpiece
best quality
hyper detailed
ultra detailed
HDR
insane detail
award winning

ORIGINALITY

Never automatically generate:

two men at a negotiation table
whiskey glasses beneath a lamp
a person holding a cat
venetian blind stripes across a face
a mafia boss behind a desk
a fedora figure in rain
a passenger viewed through a car window

Invent a different dramatic situation for every image.

MULTIPLE PROMPTS

Every requested image is independent.

Change:

woman
face
body build
hair
wardrobe
location
action
shot size
camera height
light direction
principal object
negative-space arrangement

Do not produce eight variations of one composition.

MIDJOURNEY V8.2 BASELINE

Use:

--v 8.2 --raw --ar 16:9 --s 50 --c 0 --hd

Do not automatically add a numeric SREF.

Do not automatically add --sv.

Do not use --q.

Do not use legacy --style raw.

Do not use V7 Omni Reference parameters.

STYLE REFERENCES

If the user supplies reference photographs for their aesthetic, prefer attaching those photographs to Midjourney's Style Reference slot.

Use the text prompt to describe the NEW content.

Do not describe the reference composition itself.

When using an image Style Reference, begin with:

--sw 50

If insufficient, test:

--sw 100

Increase beyond 100 only after visual comparison.

Do not add --sv merely because an image Style Reference is being used.

NUMERIC SREF RULE

Never select a numeric SREF merely because a third-party website gives it a descriptive name such as "film noir."

Only use a numeric SREF when:

1. it has been visually inspected under the intended Style Reference version;
2. it has been tested with V8.2;
3. it improves this specific photographic system;
4. it does not introduce unwanted illustration, color grading, faces, wardrobe, or composition bias.

Until such validation exists, the text controlled V8.2 Raw baseline is preferred.

PROMPT LENGTH

Target approximately 70–120 words.

Do not turn the prompt into a cinematography essay.

Prioritize:

woman
action
composition
dominant source
exact illuminated surfaces
exact dark surfaces
palette
materials
photographic finish

PARAMETERS COME LAST.

OUTPUT

Return only complete Midjourney prompts.

No explanations.

提示词：

【主题 / 作品名】：____
【核心主体】：____
【聚核方式】：人物视线 / 光线空间 / 元素回流 / Typography 密度 / 其他
【中文标题】：____
【英文标题】：____
【视觉风格】：____
【主色调】：____
【辅助色】：____
【画面比例】：9:16

生成一张具有成熟 Editorial Graphic Design 与艺术展览视觉质感的海报。

先确定一个绝对视觉核心，再让画面里的其他力量主动把视线送回这个核心。重点不是简单把主体放在中间，而是建立清晰的“向心关系”。

根据内容选择合适的聚核方式：

人物类：通过人物视线、头部朝向、身体姿态、手势和道具方向共同指向核心人物，让看不见的视线成为引导线。

空间类：通过建筑透视、墙体切面、明暗关系和光线方向，把多个空间力量汇聚到同一个焦点；主体即使很小，也能成为第一视觉。

纸本 / 拼贴类：让纸页、图像、文字条和版面碎片形成连续回流路径，外围元素有大小、疏密和方向变化，但最终都回到中央版心或核心对象。

Typography 类：通过字号、字重、字距、密度和方向变化制造向心关系；越靠近核心，文字越强、越密，外围则更轻、更疏。文字本身成为图像，而不是普通信息排版。

整张画面只保留一个主要视觉核。辅助元素只能围绕、指向、托住或平衡它，不能形成第二个同等重量的视觉中心。

Typography 必须与作品主题本身有关，不出现“视觉聚核”“构图案例”“设计研究”等模板化占位文字。让每张海报首先是一件独立成立的作品，再把构图方法藏在设计里面。

控制信息层级：主标题承担主要文字视觉；副标题和作品短句建立内容气质；日期、机构等信息集中在少量区域。避免把小字平均撒满整个版面。

保留足够负空间。可以使用裁切、叠压、透视、回流、密度变化和非对称平衡增强张力，但不要依靠箭头、明显辅助线或无意义装饰去解释构图。

整体要求：聚焦明确、主次清楚、丰富但不乱、有作品感、有成熟视觉设计品质，适合海报、展览视觉、Editorial Design 和封面设计。

面部通过赭石、灰粉、暗红与冷灰色的小块油画笔触塑造，保留冷暖交错、底色露出和边缘虚实。面部笔触较细，头发、衣料与背景更自由，呈现艺术作品印刷复制的质感，避免摄影磨皮、光滑数字渐变和全图均匀的厚涂纹理。

服饰以所填主色形成宽阔、明确的大色块，少量衣褶交代体积，其余区域逐渐转为平面装饰。让所填纹样顺着肩背、衣袖或衣褶延伸，局部跨越人物轮廓，与背景融为一体。纹样大小错落、疏密有变化，面孔附近安静，衣裙与边缘区域丰富。

以黄赭、米黄、暗铜和黑褐色绘制哑金装饰，保留色层与细微颗粒。金色面积根据主色调调整：暖金主题可以满版，深蓝、绿色或绯红主题则保留集中色块。避免镜面金属、珠宝与立体浮雕效果。

将中文展名设计成具有构图作用的巨型文字，采用修长、粗细对比明显的明朝体或宋体。根据人物位置，选择沿边纵排或横竖错落的布局，直接叠印在头发、衣裙和背景上。允许少量非关键笔画贴边裁切，但主要字形完整、准确可辨，不遮挡眼睛、鼻子和嘴部。文字颜色以米白或深黑为主，与背景形成强烈明暗对比。

顶部排列细长的英文展名，底部直接叠印副标题、日期和场馆。建立巨型中文、中型日期、紧密小型展讯三个尺度，文字组共享清楚的对齐线，不另设独立底栏。保持丰富的展讯密度，同时确保文字清晰、日期与场馆完整处于画幅内。

整体让人物面部的体积、服饰背景的平面纹样与巨字排版相互配合。缩小观看时，仍能立刻识别面孔、主色块与展名。

仅使用填写的文字，不添加随机外文、虚构赞助商、编号、四角星芒、水印、画框或展示样机。若提供参考图，吸收其笔触、字体比例与信息密度，重新创作人物和纹样。

prompts.text:
提示词：

【主题 / 活动名称】
【主色域】
【微场景】
【文化元素】
【标题文字】
【辅助信息】
【画幅比例】

设计一张具有现代东方编辑美学的文化活动海报，核心视觉采用「大色域 + 微场景」的构成方式，并加入明显但克制的纸本拼贴与水彩材质语言。

画面以大面积低饱和色块作为第一视觉主体，使用【主色域】建立强烈、完整的大形关系。色块可以通过撕纸、叠层、遮挡、围合、穿插、悬挂、斜向延伸或留白负空间构成山势、水岸、庭院、工坊、纸鸢、染布等抽象空间，但不要直接画成普通写实场景。远看首先看到清晰的大色域构图，缩略图状态下仍具有明显识别度。

所有色块具有丰富真实的手工纸、水彩纸浆和矿物颜料质感，可见天然纸纤维、颜料沉积、轻微压痕、擦印、自然浓淡变化与不规则撕纸边缘。材质细腻丰富但保持干净完整，不做脏旧、黄斑、严重破损、强颗粒或廉价复古滤镜。整体呈现哑光、自然、有呼吸感的纸本触觉。

在大片色域之间加入一个尺度非常小但内容完整的【微场景】。人物与道具整体只占画面约 2%–5%，人物正在真实地做一件事情，而不是站立摆拍。通过动作、器物和空间关系讲清一个小故事，例如放飞、弹琴、饮茶、拓印、晒书、染布、制陶等。人物服装自然克制，与整体文化主题统一，不抢夺大色域的第一视觉。

微场景可以加入少量【文化元素】，但控制数量和信息密度。道具自然散落或参与人物动作，不做商品陈列，不堆满画面。可以设置一个面积很小的暖色节点、朱红印记、灯火、月亮或器物色彩作为点睛，通常控制在画面 1%–3%。

排版采用克制的东方编辑设计语言。主标题【标题文字】使用精致的中文宋体、明朝体或具有出版感的现代字体，字号不要过大，保持充足留白，让文字成为第二视觉层级，而不是用巨大 Typography 压住画面。辅助英文、日期、地点和活动信息采用更小字号，形成清楚的信息层级。所有文字必须有真实意义，不使用 RANDOM、DESIGN、ART、STUDIO 等无意义占位词。

构图避免机械居中和规则 PPT 网格，优先使用不对称布局、大面积留白、色块错位、前后遮挡和疏密反差。让画面形成“远看简洁、有大形；近看有材质、有场景、有故事”的阅读体验。

整体风格应呈现现代东方文化海报、纸本拼贴、水彩材质、编辑设计与微型叙事融合的视觉效果，高级、自然、克制、有文化气质，同时具备真实专业海报的完成度。

避免：书籍封面既视感、巨大标题、传统水墨画、普通国风插画、写实摄影背景、PPT式排版、商业广告感、元素堆砌、过度装饰、脏旧纸张、随机噪点、塑料感、3D CGI、玻璃材质、霓虹色、Logo、水印、编号、星芒装饰。

prompts.text:
Prompt:

[POSTER THEME]: {fill in the theme}
[MAIN TITLE]: {fill in the title}
[TOP SECTION]: {portrait / object archive / typography / image}
[MIDDLE SECTION]: {information band / typography / image / transition}
[BOTTOM SECTION]: {landscape / hero object / second portrait / typography}
[COLOR PALETTE]: {fill in the palette}
[VISUAL STYLE]: {editorial / museum / photography exhibition / cultural poster}
[ASPECT RATIO]: 9:16

Create a sophisticated vertical editorial poster built around a clear three-part composition: top, middle, and bottom.

Each section must have a distinct visual role, but the final poster should feel like one continuous design rather than three stacked rectangular panels.

Use strong differences in scale, image density, typography, and negative space to establish hierarchy.

The top section should create the first visual anchor through a bold image, oversized typography, or a strong subject.

The middle section should act as the structural hinge of the composition. It can use a title, information field, narrow panoramic image, color band, or typography layer to connect the upper and lower sections.

The bottom section should provide a second visual weight or spatial conclusion through a landscape, object, secondary portrait, or oversized type.

Avoid rigid card-like boundaries. Let selected elements cross between sections through masking, overlap, irregular silhouettes, transparency, atmospheric transitions, foreground/background relationships, or typography extending beyond its original area.

Typography must actively participate in the composition rather than simply sit on top of the image. Allow large letterforms to be cropped by the page, partially hidden behind subjects, overlap imagery, or interact with negative space.

Use a strong editorial hierarchy:
one dominant title,
one clear secondary information layer,
and small meaningful metadata such as dates, venue, category, or curatorial text.

Small text should feel like real exhibition or editorial information, not decorative filler.

Keep some areas intentionally quiet. Do not fill every empty space.

The first read should communicate the main visual structure immediately.
The second read should reveal the interaction between type and imagery.
The third read should reveal the smaller information and details.

Maintain a refined contemporary poster aesthetic with strong typography, deliberate cropping, controlled information density, clean print texture, and professional editorial spacing.

Create the word "[Word]" as a readable custom font generated from the internal logic of [Math Field].

Infer the visual grammar of the chosen math field:
- symbolic notation
- proof structure
- diagrams
- recursion
- mappings
- contradiction
- symmetry
- axioms
- transformations
- equivalence relations

Convert these into glyph construction rules.

Create a finished vertical cinematic one-sheet poster for a psychological horror movie titled “THE HOLLOW ROOM.” Center the composition on a single half-open doorway at the end of a narrow, abandoned corridor; inside the room, only an unnaturally elongated human shadow is visible, cast toward the viewer even though no person stands there. Use symmetrical framing, oppressive depth, and generous negative space to make the doorway the unmistakable focal point. The corridor has cracked plaster, faded wallpaper, damp floorboards, and restrained signs of decay, rendered with believable photographic texture and perspective. Light the scene with a weak cold-blue glow leaking from the room, contrasted by one dim amber ceiling lamp. Build the palette from charcoal black, bone white, desaturated blue, and a single restrained trace of deep red beneath the door. Create tension through silence, absence, shadow, and unsettling spatial ambiguity—no gore, jump-scare face, monster reveal, or blood splatter. Place the title “THE HOLLOW ROOM” in large, widely spaced bone-white serif lettering across the lower third, clean and sharply legible against darkness. Add the short tagline “SOMETHING STAYED BEHIND.” above the title in small uppercase letters. Keep all typography precisely aligned and integrated into the composition. Polished theatrical horror key art with realistic lens logic, controlled film grain, subtle analog texture, strong visual hierarchy, and an ominous, restrained, publishable poster finish.
