where the event occurs

RELATIONSHIP
how the principal elements occupy the frame

CONSEQUENCE
what visible change proves that the event is occurring

Every major narrative statement should have a visible counterpart.

If the user describes an internal process such as cultivation, transformation, poisoning, healing, awakening or spiritual circulation, express it through observable evidence appropriate to the scene.

Possible evidence includes:

changed posture
skin or eye response
a reacting artifact
localized emission
material transformation
environmental disturbance
creature behavior
a controlled change in surrounding matter

Do not automatically expose internal anatomy, bones, organs or meridians.

Do not combine several chronological stages into one frame unless the user explicitly requests that structure.

ACTION DESIGN

Use one dominant action.

Supporting actions should explain or reinforce it.

Write physical actions with specific verbs.

Prefer:

grips
draws
turns
kneels
reaches
blocks
steps
pulls
presses
raises
catches
releases
guides
strikes
examines

Avoid replacing action with vague terms such as:

powerful
epic
dynamic
intense
majestic
dramatic
legendary

When a static image needs to suggest rapid movement, describe visible physical evidence:

cloth displaced by momentum
hair direction
debris trajectory
separated droplets
compressed stance
weapon follow-through
particles carried along a defined path

Do not use "slow motion" as a substitute for describing what the frame actually contains.

CHARACTER DESIGN

Before composing, internally establish each principal character's:

age range
body build
height impression
face shape
eye shape
brow structure
nose
mouth
skin tone
hairline
hairstyle
hair length
wardrobe silhouette
footwear
important accessories
current posture
current action

Use a small number of identifying physical features that remain readable at the chosen shot size.

Do not rely on:

beautiful
handsome
alluring
perfect
gorgeous
stunning
powerful-looking

Describe the actual features instead.

Examples:

narrow angular face
broad jaw
heavy straight brows
deep-set eyes
short uneven hair
high cheek structure
weathered skin
compact muscular build
long-limbed build

Expression should come from visible facial and bodily behavior:

eyelid tension
brow position
mouth position
jaw tension
head angle
shoulder position
breathing
grip
stance
eyeline

Do not give distant characters microscopic facial detail that cannot reasonably be visible.

ANATOMY

Maintain believable adult anatomy.

Preserve:

shoulder width
arm attachment
elbow direction
wrist continuity
pelvic orientation
knee direction
weight-bearing leg
foot placement
head and neck connection

Movement must have a physical support structure.

A strike needs stance and rotation.

A leap needs direction and body extension.

A kneeling figure needs credible hip, knee and foot placement.

A seated figure needs visible support and weight.

Do not conceal structural anatomy problems behind clothing, smoke, bloom or effects.

HANDS AND OBJECT OWNERSHIP

Every important hand must belong clearly to one arm.

Every held object must have one clear owner.

When a hand performs an important action, specify:

left or right when necessary
palm orientation
grip or finger function
object contact
direction of force

Do not assign incompatible tasks to the same hand.

Keep hands, weapons, staffs, straps, reins, pendants and creature anatomy from merging into unrelated forms.

Simplify hands that are too distant for meaningful finger detail.

HAIR

Hair must have coherent:

roots
hairline
parting
volume
direction
weight
motion

Treat dense hair as opaque.

Do not render hidden surfaces through overlapping hair.

Use fine strands only where the shot size supports them.

Avoid:

transparent hair masses
metallic strands
uniform glowing edges
excessive flyaways
crunchy strand detail
hair that ignores gravity or movement

WARDROBE

Treat clothing as constructed garments.

For each important garment establish:

type
silhouette
layering
length
fit
fabric weight
closure
major seam or panel logic
condition

Folds must follow physical causes.

GRAVITY
long hanging folds

TENSION
stretched fabric near grips, belts and fastenings

COMPRESSION
fold clusters at elbows, knees, waist and hips

MOTION
directional displacement caused by movement or wind

Wear must have a cause.

Use abrasion at contact points.

Use mud near ground contact.

Use moisture on exposed wet surfaces.

Use scorching near heat.

Use tears where stress or damage plausibly occurred.

Do not make every robe uniformly shredded.

Do not cover every garment with embroidery, gold trim, symbols, chains or ornamental hardware unless requested.

MATERIALS

Keep materials visually distinct.

SKIN
soft directional response with restrained specular highlights

WOVEN CLOTH
mostly matte with broad folds

SILK
controlled directional sheen

LEATHER
localized highlights and visible thickness

METAL
harder reflections and defined edges

WOOD
directional grain with restrained reflection

STONE
rougher diffuse response

JADE
smooth surface, internal colour depth and limited translucency

WATER
reflection, refraction and surface continuity

WET MATERIAL
stronger localized reflections without becoming uniformly glossy

Do not apply the same highlight response to every material.

Do not coat the entire image in a single elemental colour.

CREATURE DESIGN

When a creature appears, define enough physical information to stabilize its design.

Establish:

relative scale
overall silhouette
head structure
body structure
limb arrangement
wing arrangement when applicable
tail structure
horn or antler structure when applicable
surface material
colour
current behavior

A mythological name may establish the concept, but it should not replace visible design information when appearance matters.

Do not invent unsupported mythology and present it as fact.

Keep creature anatomy readable beneath supernatural effects.

Do not allow:

wings to merge with arms
horns to emerge from unrelated objects
tails to merge with weapons
human limbs to merge with creature limbs
effects to erase the creature's body structure

Give the creature a specific relationship to the event.

Possible relationships:

guards
circles
approaches
observes
guides
resists
attacks
receives
carries
responds
tracks

Do not automatically add a creature when the brief does not need one.

HUMAN AND CREATURE SCALE

State relative scale when both are important.

Use relationships such as:

creature head level with the seated character
bird wings extending beyond the character's shoulder width
beast occupying the left third of the frame
dragon body receding through the upper background
small spirit animal standing beside the character's ankle

Scale must remain consistent with perspective and depth.

Do not enlarge creatures merely to fill empty space.

SUPERNATURAL EFFECT LOGIC

Every major supernatural effect should have:

ORIGIN
where it begins

PATH
how it moves

TARGET
where it ends or what it affects

RESPONSE
what visibly changes because of contact

Example structure:

energy originates in the character's right palm
travels in a narrow arc toward the creature
contacts the creature's shoulder
nearby scales reflect the emission and loose dust moves outward from the impact

Do not use "energy everywhere."

Different phenomena need different behavior.

FIRE

Fire follows fuel, airflow and motion.

Use:

flame tongues
embers
localized smoke
heat distortion
reflected warm light
scorched surfaces

Preserve variation between bright flame cores and darker flame edges.

Do not make all nearby objects orange.

LIGHTNING

Lightning branches between defined points.

Use:

primary channel
secondary branches
brief surface illumination
localized electrical corona
material response at contact points

Keep electrical structure irregular.

Do not turn lightning into smooth glowing ribbons.

WATER AND ICE

Water should retain continuity, weight and directional flow.

Use:

sheets
streams
droplets
spray
ripples
wakes
surface reflection

Ice should show:

thickness
fracture
internal scattering
sharp or broken edges where appropriate

Do not render water and ice as blue fire.

PLANT OR WOOD ENERGY

Growth should follow physical structures.

Use:

roots
stems
vines
bark
branches
leaves
surface cracks

New growth should emerge from plausible contact points.

Do not replace plant behavior with generic green glow.

SPIRITUAL OR SPECTRAL EFFECTS

Keep spectral effects spatially organized.

Use:

localized translucent forms
defined trails
layered depth
partial materialization
controlled emission
specific interaction points

Do not fill the frame with undifferentiated fog.

TRANSFORMATION

Show transformation at a readable boundary.

Distinguish:

unchanged material
transition region
transformed material

Do not transform every surface simultaneously unless explicitly requested.

COMPOSITION

Choose a shot size that can communicate the event.

EXTREME CLOSE VIEW
Use for facial response, hand contact, an artifact or a tightly framed supernatural interaction.

CLOSE VIEW
Use for expression and a small physical action.

MEDIUM VIEW
Use for character gesture plus creature, weapon or effect relationship.

WIDE VIEW
Use for travel, environmental scale, large creatures or spatial transformation.

Do not request mutually incompatible coverage.

Do not combine an extreme close view with a complete body, enormous creature and large environment unless deliberate extreme perspective makes all three readable.

VIEWPOINT

Choose viewpoint for information, not decoration.

Possible choices:

eye level
low viewpoint
high viewpoint
profile
three-quarter view
rear three-quarter view
ground-level view
over-shoulder view

Use a Dutch angle only when instability is part of the scene.

Do not automatically use a low angle for power.

Do not automatically use a Dutch angle for action.

DEPTH

Organize depth into:

foreground
principal action plane
background

Foreground elements may frame the action, but they must not hide critical anatomy or narrative information.

Build depth through:

scale
overlap
perspective
atmospheric separation
focus hierarchy
light falloff

Use shallow depth of field only when it improves hierarchy.

Do not blur the creature, hand, weapon or effect needed to understand the event.

FRAME DIRECTION

Leave visual space in the direction of:

movement
gaze
weapon travel
creature movement
energy travel

Use diagonals when they support actual movement.

Avoid arbitrary diagonal composition language when the scene is naturally stable.

MULTIPLE CHARACTERS

For each important character define:

identity
position
action
orientation
relationship to the principal subject

Differentiate characters through:

face structure
build
height
hair
wardrobe silhouette
colour grouping
stance

Do not create clones with different hair colours.

Keep limbs and props separated.

ENVIRONMENT

Build the setting as a physical place.

Establish:

ground or floor
major structural forms
entrances or openings
vertical scale
depth boundaries
important environmental materials

Then add only the details required by the story.

CAVE
rock strata, mineral deposits, damp surfaces, debris, carved recesses where appropriate

FOREST
trunks, canopy, roots, understory, ground cover, broken light

TEMPLE
structural columns, stone or timber construction, stairs, roof or ceiling logic, weathering

MOUNTAIN
rock scale, ledges, vegetation zones, atmospheric depth

PALACE
floor material, columns, screens, doors, raised platforms, controlled ornament

RUINS
remaining structural logic first, damage second

Do not use random architecture as fantasy decoration.

ENVIRONMENTAL INTERACTION

The event must affect nearby space when appropriate.

Fire may illuminate stone.

Wind may move cloth and foliage.

Lightning may create brief hard reflections.

A heavy creature may compress soil or scatter debris.

Rain may darken fabric and create surface reflections.

A magical impact may disturb dust, water or loose vegetation.

Effects should interact with the environment rather than float independently over it.

LIGHTING

Establish one dominant source.

Define:

source type
position
direction
relative hardness
colour family
what it illuminates

Add secondary illumination only when needed.

Possible sources:

sun
overcast sky
moonlight
fire
lantern
opening in architecture
supernatural emission
reflected environmental light

Do not use contradictory lighting instructions.

Do not automatically add:

rim light
backlight
fill light
volumetric beams
glowing eyes
lens flare

Use them only when motivated.

EMISSIVE LIGHT

A luminous supernatural source must affect nearby surfaces.

Strength should decrease with distance.

Occlusion matters.

Orientation matters.

Nearby skin, cloth, metal, stone and creature surfaces should respond differently.

Do not illuminate the front of a face from a source located entirely behind the head unless another source explains it.

EXPOSURE

Protect the information required by the scene.

Dark environments may contain deep shadows without erasing the subject.

Bright supernatural effects may contain intense highlights without destroying their structure.

Keep important skin, clothing and creature features within a readable tonal range.

Avoid:

crushed shadow fields without purpose
large featureless white effects
uniform HDR brightness
milky blacks

COLOUR

Build colour from sources and materials.

Do not begin with a generic colour grade.

Use one dominant colour relationship and a limited number of secondary accents.

Examples:

amber emission against earth and charcoal
vermilion fire against dark neutral stone
forest green against neutral daylight and weathered rock
blue-white electricity against slate and muted violet
silver-blue spectral light against neutral dark materials

Keep neutral surfaces available.

Do not tint every object with the dominant effect colour.

Do not automatically use teal and orange.

ATMOSPHERE

Atmosphere must have a cause.

Possible elements:

mist
smoke
rain
dust
ash
embers
petals
snow
water spray
loose leaves
stone fragments

Define their movement when important.

Use fewer atmospheric elements when the principal action is already complex.

Do not fill empty areas with particles merely to increase detail.

DETAIL DISTRIBUTION

Place the highest useful detail on:

principal face
important hands
weapon or artifact contact
creature head or interaction point
important garment junctions

Use moderate detail on:

secondary clothing
nearby environment
supporting creature anatomy

Use lower detail on:

distant architecture
broad shadow masses
remote terrain
background atmosphere

Do not render every surface at the same information density.

IMAGE CHARACTER

The image should feel physically coherent before it feels elaborate.

Preserve:

natural body weight
material differences
clear silhouettes
controlled effects
environmental scale
localized illumination
readable action

Avoid:

plastic skin
uniform gloss
excessive sharpening
heavy chromatic aberration
random lens artifacts
constant shallow focus
particle overload
identical rim lighting on every edge
overprocessed colour
ornament added only to make the frame appear expensive

REFERENCE HANDLING

References are task-specific inputs.

Do not assume any fixed reference set, visual subject, palette, composition or genre treatment.

When references are supplied, determine what the user wants preserved.

Separate reference information into:

CONTENT
identity, object, creature, wardrobe, location or composition that should remain recognizable

STYLE
rendering, colour behavior, material treatment, lighting character and visual finish

STRUCTURE
pose, framing, spatial arrangement or perspective

Do not transfer all three categories automatically.

If the user requests style only, preserve the requested visual treatment while constructing new content and composition.

If the user requests content preservation, retain the relevant content without assuming the reference's entire style.

If the user requests structural guidance, use the relevant pose, framing or spatial relationship without copying unrelated content.

Do not describe the supplied reference itself in the finished prompt unless its visible content is intentionally part of the requested image.

STYLE REFERENCE

Use Style Reference when the user wants visual treatment transferred without requiring identity or composition preservation.

When a Style Reference is available in the actual Midjourney workflow, allow it to carry broad stylistic information.

Keep the text prompt focused on:

new subject
new action
new environment
new spatial relationships
necessary material behavior
necessary effect behavior

Do not redundantly describe every stylistic property already supplied by a strong reference.

Do not treat Style Reference as an identity lock.

CONTENT PRESERVATION AND EDITING

When exact identity, creature design, object design or existing composition must remain stable, use an applicable reference or editing workflow rather than expecting descriptive text alone to provide exact continuity.

Do not invent unsupported Midjourney reference syntax.

Do not claim that a reference guarantees exact identity or geometry.

ORIGINALITY

When the user requests a new scene, construct new:

action
blocking
environment
viewpoint
effect geometry
lighting arrangement

Do not automatically recycle familiar cultivation imagery such as:

outstretched palm casting
floating cross-legged meditation
bird directly behind a shoulder
dragon circling overhead
glowing eyes
energy vortex around the body
robe blowing toward the camera
debris flying at the lens

Use these only when the brief actually calls for them.

Do not make every cultivator young, slender, attractive, richly dressed or combat-oriented.

Do not add mythological creatures, weapons or magical effects without narrative purpose.

LANGUAGE CONTROL

Use concrete visual language.

Prefer:

"she braces the spear shaft against her left forearm"

instead of:

"she wields the spear powerfully"

Prefer:

"three electrical branches connect the spear tip to the creature's lower jaw"

instead of:

"epic lightning energy explodes everywhere"

Prefer:

"heavy brown linen robe, frayed at the cuffs and darkened by damp soil"

instead of:

"ultra-detailed ancient mystical robe"

Remove words that do not change visible

prompts.text:
Another hybrid style. AI picked the topics. Visualized by GPT 2.5

2x2 grid, 16:9, do this for 4 days that changed history: INPUT: $ SUBJECT

// 01 — SEMANTIC EXTRACTION
 
S = infer($ SUBJECT)

IDENTITY = {
    archetype       : dominant_persona_or_form(S),
    symbols         : 8..16 culturally meaningful symbols(S),
    places          : 2..5 relevant environments_or_landmarks(S),
    objects         : 4..10 iconic objects(S),
    achievements    : 3..7 defining ideas/events(S),
    tensions        : opposing forces / contradictions(S),
    physical_anchor : one ordinary real-world object that can
                      metaphorically represent S,
    title           : shortest recognizable name(S),
    motto           : infer_concise_phrase(S)
}

// 02 — BUILD THE MONUMENTAL TOTEM

Create ONE tall frontal figure/silhouette representing S.

The silhouette must read instantly from a distance.

Divide vertically:

        HEAD
          ↓
    IDEAS / MIND
          ↓
      IDENTITY
          ↓
      ACHIEVEMENTS
          ↓
      PLACE / ROOTS
          ↓
       LEGACY

But do NOT use literal labeled boxes.

Instead fill the body with a dense symbolic collage.

Example transformation:

portrait.face
    → angular mask / emblem

torso
    → architecture + books + diagrams + machines

arms
    → tools / actions / symbols

lower body
    → landscapes / crowds / infrastructure / history

base
    → strongest legacy symbol

// 03 — PHYSICAL-OBJECT BREACH

Introduce ONE unexpected tangible object derived from
IDENTITY.physical_anchor.

It should break out of the otherwise flat poster.

Examples of behavior:

real feather inserted into drawn history
real key crossing an illustrated body
real lightbulb replacing a drawn sun
real thread connecting symbolic regions
real leaf emerging from printed architecture
real ruler crossing a scientific composition
real folded paper object projecting outward

RULE:

only ONE physical intrusion.

Everything else remains printed / illustrated.

The physical object must have semantic meaning,
not merely decoration.

// 04 — ENGINEERED TYPOGRAPHY

Set IDENTITY.title beneath or beside the figure.

Typography is custom-built from subject logic.

Each letter may inherit:

    trajectories
    architecture
    tools
    machines
    anatomical forms
    landscape contours
    scientific diagrams
    cultural ornaments

Do not use a normal font unchanged.

Example:

if S = aviation:
    letter stems → wings / fuselage geometry

if S = music:
    counters → sound waves / strings

if S = astronomy:
    crossbars → orbital paths

if S = architecture:
    letter skeleton → structural beams

if S = biology:
    curves → cellular / botanical structures

// 05 — STYLE FIELD

STYLE =
    WPA-era civic poster
    × mid-century linocut
    × symbolic editorial portrait
    × museum identity panel
    × industrial typography study
    × subtle trompe-l'œil object intervention

PALETTE:
    warm cream paper
    charcoal black
    muted brick red
    desaturated olive
    optional one subject-specific accent

PRINT:
    coarse ink
    rubbed edges
    imperfect registration
    subtle paper fibers
    faded screenprint
    engraving hatch

FIGURE:
    severe frontal symmetry
    simplified geometry
    slightly elongated proportions
    emotionally restrained expression

BACKGROUND:
    faint oversized halo / sun disc / map / flag / diagram
    inferred from subject.

// 06 — COMPOSITION

              ◯
          ┌────────┐
          │  FACE  │
          │symbols │
          │objects │────── REAL OBJECT
          │places  │
          │history │
          └────────┘

            SUBJECT
        concise motto

Use abundant negative space around the monument.

No modern UI.
No gradients.
No glossy CGI.
No random decorative symbols.
Every mark must connect to $ SUBJECT.

OUTPUT:
a ceremonial symbolic portrait where an entire subject's
identity is compressed into one monumental human/totemic
form, interrupted by one physically real metaphor and
finished with custom engineered typography.

prompts.text:
Prompt:

Create a charming Japanese-style bakery poster combining photorealistic food photography, playful hand-drawn illustrations, and nostalgic editorial typography.

CUSTOMIZE
- Brand: [Brand Name]
- Food: [Main Food / Products]
- Concept: [Miniature World / Floating Food / Flavor Guide / Cozy Scene]
- Headline: [Japanese or English Title]
- Tagline: [Short Catchy Phrase]
- Details: [Flavors / Product Info / Event Details]
- Color Palette: [Preferred Colors]
- Year: [2026 or Custom]
- Aspect Ratio: 9:16

VISUAL STYLE

Japanese indie bakery aesthetics with a warm, playful, slightly nostalgic editorial feel. Combine realistic food photography with delicate, imperfect pen-and-ink illustrations.

Use cream-colored paper backgrounds, cocoa-brown lettering, soft natural colors, and subtle print textures.

FOOD & STORYTELLING

Make the food the visual centerpiece, with appetizing textures, golden crusts, natural imperfections, soft daylight, and realistic shadows.

Add a few tiny 2D hand-drawn characters interacting with the food—walking across pastries, exploring oversized treats, or enjoying a cozy café moment.

Create a charming miniature story through simple, meaningful interactions.

COMPOSITION & TYPOGRAPHY

Choose a distinctive layout based on the concept: oversized food, floating arrangements, asymmetrical product displays, or cozy still-life scenes.

Maintain a strong focal point, balanced visual hierarchy, and approximately 35–40% clean negative space.

Use expressive Japanese-style handwritten headlines, elegant retro serif fonts, and small playful annotations.

Keep all text accurate, readable, and naturally integrated into the design.

FINAL ART DIRECTION

The finished poster should feel like a professionally designed Japanese bakery advertisement—warm, whimsical, visually engaging, and commercially polished.

Keep illustrations minimal and purposeful. Let the food, typography, and storytelling create the visual impact.

Avoid excessive doodles, cluttered layouts, CGI-looking food, 3D cartoon characters, random text, heavy distressing, decorative sparkles, numbering, and watermarks.

Generate one complete, standalone vertical poster, not a collage or mockup.

title: Miniature World / Floating Food / Flavor Guide / Cozy Scene

prompts.text:
Prompt:

TITLE: [your main word]
PROJECT NAME: [brand / exhibition / campaign]
ARCHITECTURAL STRUCTURE: [vertical fins / separated buildings / staggered platforms / folded planes / other]
TYPE MECHANISM: [slice / span / offset / fold / custom]
SUBJECT: [small human figure / none]
ACCENT COLOR: [one strong solid color]
SUPPORTING TEXT: [location / date / short tagline]
FORMAT: 9:16 vertical poster

Create a high-impact perspective typography poster where oversized type is physically integrated into architecture and only becomes visually complete from one intentional camera viewpoint.

Build the architectural structure first, then let the typography strictly follow its real depth, surfaces, angles, gaps, folds and occlusion.

Depending on the selected mechanism, the word can be sliced across multiple vertical planes, span a physical gap between structures, break across staggered platforms, or continue over folded architectural surfaces.

The main word should occupy roughly 35–55% of the composition. Individual fragments may look abstract or incomplete on separate surfaces, but from the intended viewpoint they should visually align into one clear, readable word.

Use bold geometric sans-serif typography with one strong solid accent color against restrained architectural materials such as concrete, black, white or neutral stone.

If a person is included, keep them small and use them mainly as a scale reference. Let architecture naturally hide or overlap part of the figure so they feel physically inside the typographic space.

Add only a small amount of editorial information such as project name, location, date and one short thematic line.

Overall style: perspective typography, spatial graphic design, contemporary architecture, editorial poster, anamorphic installation, strong depth and clean hierarchy.

Avoid floating text, random distortion, weak alignment, decorative 3D extrusion, neon sci-fi effects, excessive filler copy, cluttered backgrounds, watermarks and numbering.

prompts.text:
提示词：

【主题】：填写，例如「风迹 / 汲泉 / 苔庭 / 松间」
【中文主标题】：填写 2–4 个字
【英文标题】：填写
【自然主题元素】：填写，例如风、水、苔藓、松木、山石、草穗
【前景立体实物】：填写，例如石钵、苔石、枯木、薄纸、植物
【摄影窗口场景】：填写，例如雾中山林、山涧、草坡、松林
【主色调】：填写低饱和自然色
【画幅比例】：默认 9:16

生成一张东方自然文化主题的 Editorial Design 艺术海报。

整体采用暖象牙米白艺术纸背景，保留轻微天然纸纤维与克制的印刷颗粒，大面积留白，画面安静、自然、松弛、有文化感。

画面上方或偏右放置巨大的中文手写书法标题【中文主标题】，使用自由、真实、有毛笔提按变化与墨迹浓淡的现代东方书写方式，让中文大字本身成为主要视觉锚点。

搭配纤细优雅的英文 Serif 字体呈现【英文标题】，再加入少量有实际意义的中文短句、英文说明和日期信息，形成“大书法 + 英文标题 + 小字号编辑文字”的信息层级。

画面中部加入一个大型低饱和自然色块，颜色使用【主色调】。色块边缘具有自然撕纸、山体、地形或有机形态感，保持完整清晰的大形，不要拆成大量碎片。

在色块内部开出一个圆形、椭圆形、竖向或不规则自然窗口，窗口中呈现【摄影窗口场景】的真实摄影画面。摄影区域低对比、低饱和、有薄雾和空气透视感，像透过纸张开孔看见另一个真实自然空间。

画面下部加入真实立体的【前景立体实物】，具有真实材质、体积、接触阴影和自然空间关系。

Prompt:

Brand: [BRAND NAME]

Subject: [PERSON / PRODUCT / BOTH]
Motion Type: [SWING / FLEX / FLIP / ROLL / OTHER]
Main Color: [COLOR]
Accent Color: [COLOR]

Use realistic commercial photography, oversized typography, strong perspective, vivid color contrast, and contemporary editorial design.

Make the main word extremely large and give it one clear physical behavior:

 SWING: suspend the letters and let them move like swinging gates while the subject passes between them.
 FLEX: let the letter surface bend smoothly under the subject’s weight, then visibly rebound.
 FLIP: rotate different letters around simple pivot axes and reveal a contrasting back surface.
 ROLL: turn a round letter into a rolling typographic form that moves through the scene and interacts with real wheels or objects.

The subject must physically react to the typography through stepping, dodging, balancing, riding, or making contact with it.

Keep the typography clearly readable. Use clean matte surfaces, even colors, sharp edges, and controlled depth. Avoid rough concrete, distressed textures, scratches, dirt, random noise, and heavy 3D architecture.

All motion arcs, guide lines, callout lines, and curves must be smooth, continuous, and clearly rendered.

Keep people highly realistic with natural anatomy, believable proportions, real skin texture, controlled highlights, detailed hair, and authentic clothing materials. Avoid waxy skin, oily reflections, CGI appearance, distorted limbs, oversized hands or feet, and extreme wide angle deformation.

Use one dominant high impact color, one contrasting accent color, and black or white for balance. Add only a few meaningful campaign details such as the brand name, product name, slogan, and 2 to 3 short feature callouts.

The final image should feel like a finished campaign key visual where typography, motion, and the subject behave as one physical system.

Avoid generic subject plus big text layouts, random motion effects, broken lines, unreadable typography, cluttered UI, rough materials, unrealistic anatomy, and meaningless filler text.

左右元素不只是装饰，而要真正参与方向感和节奏。可以使用桨阵、骨架、弓身、声波、羽翼、杆件等形成连续视觉序列，通过重复、放射、倾斜和尺度变化制造动势。

画面要有一个非常清楚的第一视觉大形：中央硬轴 + 两侧方向性结构。左右视觉重量保持平衡，但不要机械镜像，允许角度、尺度、材质和节奏存在变化。

Typography 根据主体方向重新设计，可以横跨结构、贴近硬轴、沿大形排布或局部错位，不要固定使用四字纵排、巨大单字居中或同一种标题模板。

可加入一个很小的结构研究模块，例如动作阶段、受力、波纹、骨架或路径示意，面积控制在 5%–7%，增加“设计研究感”，但不要做成 PPT 或教学图。

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色，使用明确的大色域和强主体反差。

第一眼看到大形和动势，第二眼看到中轴和标题，第三眼发现两侧元素如何共同制造方向与张力。

避免：机械对称、重复元素完全复制、主体过小、方向混乱、多个视觉中心、复杂技术参数、PPT 信息框、随机装饰线、过度做旧、斑驳噪点和低完成度 AI 海报感。

生成一张具有强空间关系与成熟 Editorial Design 气质的「中轴夹景」文化海报。

先建立一个清楚的中央阅读区域，再让左右两侧元素通过真实关系共同形成中轴。两侧不只是做装饰性对称，而要真正参与主题表达。

可以根据题材选择不同关系：

人物对望：利用人物姿态、衣袖、操杆或视线共同夹出中央灯幕或焦点；

轮廓围合：利用伞面、建筑、器物或自然边缘围出雨巷、道路、天空等纵深空间；

正反穿透：使用同一对象的正反两面，并通过针、线、杆件等真实结构穿过中央，将两侧连接；

线性交织：让两组不同方向的线条在中央相遇，从独立线性元素逐渐形成完整织物、纹样或表面。

中轴不一定是一条色带，它可以是一块发光区域、一条纵深路径、一根真实针线、一段正在形成的织物，甚至是一块被两侧轮廓共同围出的负空间。

左右视觉重量保持平衡，但禁止机械镜像。可以通过颜色、姿态、材质、尺度和轮廓制造明显差异，只要两侧最终都把注意力推向中央。

Typography 根据每张主题重新设计，可横排、错位、跨区、贴近轮廓或与真实主体轻微穿插。不要固定使用四字纵排、中央巨大单字或同一种标题模板。

信息集中在 2–3 个区域，可加入一个面积约 5%–7% 的小型研究节点，例如动作轨迹、结构关系、针迹、开合状态或经纬组织，让画面更像成熟的文化展览视觉，而不是普通装饰海报。

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色，优先使用明确的大色域和材质反差。

第一眼看到左右主体与中央关系；第二眼读到标题；第三眼发现人物、空间或线条究竟如何参与构图。

整体要求：高清、干净、结构明确、信息丰富但集中，具有 Museum Exhibition Poster × Contemporary Editorial Graphic Design × East Asian Cultural Visual 气质。

Prompt:

Create a 9:16 vertical poster series in English, with a high-end editorial style inspired by brutalist architecture, monumental perspective typography, realistic human figures, and three-dimensional spatial graphics.

The overall visual system should feel bold, clean, architectural, and sophisticated. Use a dramatic low-angle perspective so the architecture, typography, human figure, and spatial form all belong to the same perspective system. Keep the buildings monumental and geometric, with raw warm-gray concrete, a deep cobalt-blue sky, warm ivory typography, charcoal clothing, and safety orange as the only strong accent color.

The typography should be oversized, tall, condensed, and visually integrated into the structure. It should feel embedded in the space rather than simply placed on top of the image. Human figures should look like realistic young adults, naturally posed, with believable skin texture, clothing folds, and proportions. Add meaningful editorial microcopy, secondary headlines, and small annotations with a clean hierarchy.

Poster 1: SKY PRISM
Create a monumental cantilevered concrete platform with a realistic young man seated near the edge. Build a large transparent triangular prism around and behind him, combining clear faces, thin white edges, and one orange translucent plane. Place the main title “SKY PRISM” across the sky in huge perspective typography. Add secondary text such as “THREE PLANES”, “LIGHT / MASS”, and “BETWEEN EDGES”. The image should feel airy, sharp, architectural, and spatially layered.

Poster 2: CUT SPACE
Create a strong brutalist concrete wall with a projecting platform and a realistic young woman standing near the outer edge. Insert a thick diagonal orange spatial slice cutting through the architecture and the typographic space. Place the main title “CUT SPACE” in giant warm-ivory letters across the blue sky, with parts interrupted by the orange slice. Add secondary text such as “SHIFT THE MASS”, “BREAK THE PLANE”, and “THROUGH THE EDGE”. The composition should feel bold, structural, and aggressive.

Poster 3: TYPE SPAN
Create two massive concrete structures separated by an open gap. Bridge them with giant three-dimensional letters spelling “SPAN”, with warm-ivory front faces and orange side depth, so the word itself functions as architecture. A realistic young woman walks across the top of the letters. Place the word “TYPE” in huge perspective typography across the sky. Add secondary text such as “WORDS CARRY WEIGHT”, “CROSS THE GAP”, and “BUILT TO CONNECT”. The composition should clearly show that the word becomes a bridge.

Poster 4: OPEN SEQUENCE
Create a long sequence of repeated concrete portal frames receding into the distance with strong one-point perspective. A realistic young woman walks through the structure, giving the space scale and rhythm. Integrate the title “OPEN SEQUENCE” across the frames and sky. Add secondary text such as “PASSAGE FIELD”, “FRAME AFTER FRAME”, and “KEEP GOING”. Use small orange accents inside the architecture to reinforce depth and progression. The image should feel spacious, graphic, and cinematic.

All four posters should belong to the same visual family while each one explores a different relationship between architecture, typography, human scale, and spatial intervention.

title: that the word becomes a bridge

An adult woman sitting directly on an outdoor red athletics track, photographed as a vertical 3:4 full-body environmental portrait. The photographer is positioned noticeably above and in front of her, looking downward at roughly a 30–45 degree angle from some physical distance, as if the image had been casually taken from the edge of the stands or another elevated position beside the track. Use a mild telephoto or smartphone-telephoto visual language, roughly 70–120mm full-frame equivalent, producing gentle spatial compression. Avoid eye-level framing and avoid the polished look of a commercial fitness campaign.  She sits on the track with one leg extended diagonally a long distance toward the lower-left foreground while the other leg opens sideways toward the right and bends naturally. Her hips and upper thighs rest directly on the rubber surface, her torso leans slightly forward, and her shoulders hang loosely rather than being deliberately pulled back. One hand reaches toward the extended shoe area while the other remains beside the bent leg, appearing to hold or adjust another running shoe. The pose should feel like something that happened after a run, stretch, or training set rather than something designed specifically for the camera.  Her body is slim and lightly athletic, with long arms and legs and subtle functional muscle definition rather than exaggerated fitness-model musculature. Her abdomen and waist remain exposed; the waist is relatively narrow and the stomach naturally flat, but preserve small soft-tissue changes caused by sitting rather than forcing a sculpted six-pack or extreme hourglass proportions. Visible skin includes parts of the face, neck, shoulders, collarbones, upper chest, both arms, abdomen, side waist, and most of both thighs, while the lower legs are largely covered by white knee-high athletic socks.  Her skin is fair to light with a neutral undertone, becoming slightly gray-rose in the diffused daylight rather than orange or deeply golden. Keep real fine skin texture, slight tonal irregularity, subtle pores, and an almost imperceptible post-exercise sheen across the shoulders, arms, and legs. The tactile impression should be smooth and naturally warm from physical activity, with only a faint surface moisture rather than glossy retouching or plastic skin.  She wears a simple black low-neck sports bra with moderately wide straps and matte stretch fabric, fully supporting and covering the bust while naturally exposing the collarbones, upper chest, and a small amount of skin within the neckline. Her bottoms are loose short black athletic shorts with a relaxed side opening or slit and a tiny white logo on one side. The shorts should bunch, shift, and wrinkle naturally because of the seated position; do not replace them with tight yoga shorts.  She wears white knee-high athletic socks and white, black, and gray running shoes. Preserve the impression that one shoe is worn while another shoe is being held or adjusted beside the bent leg. Add a black square smartwatch on one wrist, a very fine necklace with a tiny pendant, and a small amount of finger jewelry.  Her deep-black to very dark brown hair is gathered into a loose low ponytail. Irregular airy bangs fall over the forehead, with fine side strands framing the cheeks and jaw. Her hair looks slightly disturbed by training: some bangs lightly adhere to the skin, the ponytail is relaxed rather than perfectly neat, and several strands kick outward. She wears narrow dark sunglasses that conceal most of her eyes, so do not invent exaggerated eyes or unusual iris colors. Her lips remain relaxed or slightly parted, without an obvious smile. Makeup is minimal and low-saturation, with a lightweight complexion and muted natural rose or dusty-pink lips rather than heavy contour or glamour styling.  The background is almost entirely the muted brick-red to gray-red rubber running track. Several white lane markings travel diagonally across the frame, creating natural perspective and strong geometric lines. Retain the fine granular rubber texture, tiny pale specks, dust, and subtle wear marks. Do not add spectators, stadium buildings, trees, or visually complicated scenery. A large amount of empty track surrounding the subject is essential to the identity of the composition.  Use soft overcast or thin-cloud daylight, with broad skylight falling evenly from above and slightly in front of her. Create wide, low-contrast highlights across the shoulders, collarbones, upper chest, thighs, and knees, while the undersides of the body and folds in the clothing naturally darken. There should be no hard-edged shadows, golden-hour glow, warm orange skin, professional fill light, or dramatic rim lighting. Keep the running track slightly desaturated and dusty brick red rather than vivid synthetic scarlet.  Retain moderate digital sharpness, subtle telephoto compression, faint social-media image compression, and optionally extremely fine grain. Keep the woman clearly focused while the more distant track softens only slightly; because the background is a flat track surface, avoid exaggerated creamy bokeh.  She had just finished part of her training and had already dropped into a recovery stretch, still adjusting her shoe and catching her breath. The photographer pressed the shutter from above just as she lifted her face toward the camera. It feels like an unprepared instant that remained for only a second before she would return to stretching. The final mood should feel tired, quiet, cool, slightly solitary, and casually observational—an athletic social-media candid rather than a polished campaign.  Negative prompt: indoor gym, running pose, standing pose, eye-level camera, low-angle shot, golden hour, warm orange light, studio rim light, polished fitness advertisement, exaggerated muscles, bodybuilder physique, extreme hourglass body, tiny waist, plastic skin, poreless skin, heavy glamour makeup, bright lipstick, big smile, perfect hair, perfect symmetry, oversaturated red track, clean commercial background, extreme bokeh, beauty close-up.

Create an authentic 2:3 vertical digital portrait shot from a distinctly elevated downward angle. The subject is a clearly adult young woman in her twenties. Position the camera roughly 25–40 degrees above her eye level and point it downward while she actively leans her upper body toward the camera and raises her face to look directly into the lens.

She has a compact soft oval face, a natural jawline, relatively large deep-brown eyes, and a fine straight nose. Preserve subtle facial asymmetry rather than turning her into an idealized perfectly symmetrical face. She is caught in a genuinely cheerful moment: her mouth is naturally open in a broad laugh, neat bright teeth clearly visible, mouth corners strongly lifted, and the apples of her cheeks pushed upward by the smile. It should feel as though the photographer has just made her laugh rather than like a carefully held commercial expression.

Use a bright beauty look inspired by Japanese swimsuit photobooks and contemporary East Asian magazine makeup: soft dark-brown brows, a thin dark eyeliner line extending subtly at the outer corners, long curled lashes with definition but no extreme volume, very pale peach-brown or pink-brown eyeshadow, and delicate brightness beneath the eyes. Add translucent peach-pink blush across the apples of the cheeks, a soft highlight along the nose, and glossy coral-rose lips with realistic wet reflections. Keep the foundation thin and luminous. Mild consumer-camera beauty processing is acceptable, but the face must still retain believable human skin.

Her hair is natural black to dark brown-black and pulled into a low or mid-low ponytail. The crown and sides are sleek, smooth, and close to the scalp with soft blue-black flash reflections. Use a loose side part with thin elongated fringe pieces across the forehead and several delicate face-framing strands near the temples and cheeks. The ponytail itself should not look salon-perfect: let the ends remain slightly fluffy, uneven, and casually messy.

Her upper body is slim with soft natural lines, and the elevated perspective visually compresses the torso as she leans toward the lens. She wears a white triangle string swimsuit top, with thin straps running around the neck and tying behind it, small triangular cups connected by fine strings, and additional white ties visible along the side or rear. Preserve a tiny red logo or graphic accent on the white fabric. The material should be thin, body-following, and mostly matte with slightly brighter edges under flash. Do not turn it into padded lingerie, lace underwear, or a sports top.

Visible skin includes the full face, ears, neck, shoulders, collarbones, arms, raised palm and fingers, exposed upper-chest skin surrounding the swimsuit, and a small amount of upper abdomen and side torso. The legs, buttocks, and complete waist and hips remain outside the frame. The chest region is covered by the swimsuit and appears visually prominent mainly because of the forward lean, elevated angle, and short shooting distance; keep the anatomy natural and do not exaggerate proportions.

A crucial compositional feature is one open hand raised beside the face, palm facing the lens, with all five fingers spread apart. The hand sits significantly closer to the camera than the face, so a short wide lens must create clear foreshortening: the palm and fingers appear intentionally oversized, especially as they enter from the upper-left edge. Do not correct the hand to normal scale—the exaggerated near-far perspective is part of the image's identity.

Her skin is fair neutral-to-warm creamy ivory with subtle peach-pink blood tone. It should visually feel soft, silky, and lightly coated with sunscreen or thin foundation. The cheeks are especially fine and smooth, while the shoulders, collarbones, and upper chest have a soft satin quality. The palm should retain faint natural skin lines. Preserve tiny pores and minor tone differences rather than rendering completely textureless AI skin.

Use a direct cool-white flash or bright LED positioned very close to the camera axis, slightly above the lens, around 5000K–5800K. This creates short shallow shadows and bright but soft highlights across the forehead, nose bridge, nose tip, upper cheeks, collarbones, shoulder caps, and upper chest. The raised palm, being closer to the light source, should appear slightly brighter. Warm beige stone nearby reflects a small amount of warm fill back onto her skin, creating creamy warmth without making the image orange.

The background consists of large cream-beige and pale sand-colored stone or ceramic wall tiles, with clear horizontal and vertical grout lines and subtle mottled natural-stone variation. Keep the environment simple. Do not invent an elaborate pool, beach, hotel room, or furniture. The wall should be a little darker than the subject but still detailed enough that its stone texture remains visible.

The photographic rendering should resemble a wide smartphone main camera, compact digital camera, or short-distance direct-flash portrait, approximately 24–30mm equivalent. Avoid telephoto compression. The face, raised hand, upper body, hair, and much of the wall should remain fairly sharp, with medium-to-deep depth of field rather than creamy shallow bokeh. Retain mild computational sharpening, skin brightening, subtle beauty-camera smoothing, and believable flash sheen.

Keep the composition imperfect and energetic: the head sits near the upper part of the frame, the spread palm intrudes boldly from the upper-left, the torso leans forward, and the shoulders form a slight diagonal rather than a perfectly horizontal pose.

She had just moved closer to the camera. She is now laughing upward toward the elevated lens while holding her spread hand beside her face, with the ponytail still carrying a trace of the movement that just happened. A second later, she will probably lower her hand and let the exaggerated smile relax.

The final image should feel bright, cheerful, playful, interactive, and unmistakably photographic, blending 2000s–2010s Japanese digital swimsuit-photobook energy with the crispness of a modern consumer camera.

Find the precise visual intersection of these four concepts.

Ignore the literal technological terminology
and subject matter in the references.

Create an extraordinary experimental typographic
wordmark for $ SUBJECT.

If the subject represents:

Use directional strokes, displacement, repeated
contours, kinetic breaks, and rhythmic geometry.

NATURE:
Translate growth, branching, organic repetition,
and environmental forms into letter anatomy.

SCIENCE:
Use scientific geometry, orbital paths, schematic

OTHER SUBJECTS:

Surprisingly intelligent up close.
Immediately recognizable.
Distinctly original.

Illustration Style:
Naive black ink drawings, irregular pencil strokes, playful proportions, charmingly imperfect characters, and occasional delicate stitched details.

Keep the illustration simple, expressive, and full of personality. Avoid overly polished digital artwork or uniform embroidery textures.

Composition & Typography:
Use one oversized illustrated subject, a striking realistic food element, generous negative space, and an asymmetrical Japanese editorial layout.

Place a bold magazine title at the top. Integrate the headline and minimal supporting text naturally around the illustration, allowing typography and handdrawn lines to interact.

Texture & Color:
Soft linen paper, subtle fabric fibers, matte printing, muted earthy colors, and gentle natural lighting. Let the realistic food provide the strongest color accent.

Art Direction:
Whimsical, nostalgic, handcrafted, slightly eccentric, yet sophisticated.

Prioritize visual surprise, clear silhouettes, expressive linework, and thoughtful negative space.

Avoid glossy CGI, vector cartoons, excessive decorations, dense text, random lettering, cluttered backgrounds, copied branding, artist signatures, and watermarks.

提示词：

【海报主题】：{填写主题}
【中文主标题】：{填写标题}
【英文标题】：{填写英文名称}
【核心视觉创意】：{如巨鲸背着书港、茶叶化作茶山、雨伞撑起城市}
【主要画面元素】：{建筑、自然、人物、植物、器物等}
【配色方案】：{主色、辅助色、强调色}
【活动信息】：{日期、地点、副标题、活动内容等}
【画幅比例】：9:16

创作一张具有东亚复古手绘美学的文化活动艺术海报，融合日本与台湾地区独立文化展览海报、复古绘本插画、传统平面印刷和实验性编辑设计的视觉语言。

视觉创意与构图

围绕主题创造一个充满想象力的微缩世界。让日常器物、建筑、植物、自然景观和人物通过尺度变化、形态融合或超现实组合，形成独特而完整的视觉隐喻。

主体必须拥有醒目的大形体与清晰轮廓，可通过环绕、穿插、叠合、局部压角或蜿蜒路径组织画面。

主体内部包含丰富而有意义的生活细节，外围保留自然留白。远看具有强烈的图形识别度，近看能发现有趣的故事。

手绘风格与色彩

采用自由、不完全规整的手绘墨线，结合二维平涂、局部精细线描和艺术化造型。

线条具有自然粗细变化，建筑、树木和人物允许适度夸张、不对称和轻微稚拙感。部分形体使用深色描边，部分直接由完整色块构成，避免机械工整。

以干净温暖的象牙米白纸张为底，搭配草木绿、湖水青、陶土橙、芥末黄、炭黑等复古自然色。

每张海报选择2–3种主要颜色，并用一种醒目的强调色建立视觉焦点。颜色饱满、平涂均匀，保留极轻微的传统印刷质感，避免厚重颗粒与过度做旧。

文字与编辑排版

使用大胆、富有手绘笔触的中文大标题，结合复古英文衬线字体、醒目日期数字和精致的小字号活动信息。

采用不对称、富有节奏的编辑式排版，让文字与插画产生围合、穿插、遮挡或空间呼应，而非简单覆盖在画面上。

标题、日期、地点、活动说明应形成清晰的信息层级。所有文字具有实际意义，构成完整、专业的文化活动海报。

整体质量要求

画面具有成熟独立插画师的原创艺术气质，兼具自由的手绘趣味、鲜活的平面色彩、超现实想象力与专业排版。

保持统一的系列美学，但允许不同主题拥有独立的构图、色彩和视觉创意。

避免普通儿童卡通、3D微缩模型、CG渲染、照片写实、复杂渐变、过度精致的商业插画、随机装饰、无意义文字、四角星芒和模板化排版。

最终输出一张完整、精致、具有收藏价值的9:16高清竖版艺术海报。

Prompt:

【主题】：____
【四字中文标题】：____

【主体表现方式】：摄影 / 插画 / 版画 / 拼贴 / 混合媒介

【点缀色】：____
【日期 / 机构 / 辅助信息】：____
【画面比例】：9:16

生成一张具有成熟文化展览与编辑设计气质的「压角构图」海报。核心视觉由一个强主体、巨型中文 Typography、边缘信息和留白共同组成，让文字不只是标题，而是真正成为画面的边界和构图结构。

主体占画面约 45%–60%，保持完整、有明确轮廓和视觉重量，不要为了构图故意扭曲或切碎。根据主题选择真实摄影、版画、插画或混合媒介表现，并让主体本身具备足够强的识别度和作品感。

将【四字中文标题】拆开分布在画面四角或边缘，但不要四字等大、等距、完全对称。选择 1–2 个字作为主要压力点，大幅放大并局部裁出画面；其余文字作为次级回应。允许主体与大字发生真实穿插，例如人物、动物、器物、浪花、枝条或衣袖从字形前后穿过，让“字在主体后面、主体又从字中长出来”，形成丰富的前后空间关系。

英文标题、日期、机构、说明文字集中在 2–3 个边缘区域，可混合横排、竖排和极小字号。通过超大中文、中号英文、极小信息形成强烈字号反差，不要把所有小字排成整齐栏目，也不要平均撒满全图。

整张图只使用一套与主题直接相关的辅助纹样，例如面具主题使用鼓点放射纹，山野主题使用角形或植物线稿，海洋主题使用波浪纹，风物主题使用风线。辅助纹样可以重复、放大、裁边或淡化，但不要同时加入多套无关装饰。

背景不能完全空白，可加入极淡纸张纹理、印刷颗粒、主题线稿、图案残影或少量档案信息，让留白“有内容”，但远看仍然保持主体清晰。

色彩控制在 3–4 个主要颜色，建立明确色彩立场。主体、巨字和背景之间要有足够反差，同时避免过多颜色互相竞争。

整体阅读顺序必须清楚：
第一眼看到强主体和巨型压角文字；
第二眼发现主体与文字之间的遮挡、穿插和异形关系；
第三眼才阅读英文、日期和辅助信息。

目标效果：东亚文化展览海报、编辑设计、艺术出版物感；信息丰富但不乱，大字、主体和留白互相咬合，边缘有压力、中心有聚焦。即使去掉所有小字，画面本身仍然应该是一件完整成立的视觉作品。

prompts.text:
Prompt:

Create a bold editorial campaign poster where oversized typography behaves like a physical material instead of remaining flat and static.

Brand: [BRAND NAME]
Product / Campaign: [PRODUCT OR CAMPAIGN]
Main Word: [SHORT WORD]
Subject: [PERSON / PRODUCT / BOTH]
Material Behavior: [FOLD / PEEL / SPLIT / REFLECT / OTHER]
Main Color: [COLOR]
Accent Color: [COLOR]
Campaign Details: [SLOGAN / SPECS / DATE]
Aspect Ratio: [9:16]

Use realistic commercial photography, oversized typography, strong high-contrast colors, and contemporary editorial design.

Make the main word extremely large, filling roughly 50–75% of the composition. Let the typography physically react according to the selected material behavior:

 FOLD: create clean creases and folded planes that follow the product or subject’s structural direction.
 PEEL: build several clean color layers and let the top layer lift away to reveal what is underneath.
 SPLIT: divide the typography into several large strips and shift them in alternating directions while keeping the subject visually intact.
 REFLECT: turn the letterforms into flat mirrored surfaces that realistically reflect the subject, product, and surrounding colors.

Create strong foreground–subject–background interaction so the person or product feels physically connected to the typography.

Use one dominant color with black, white, and one contrasting accent color. Add only a few meaningful campaign details such as the brand name, product name, slogan, specifications, or small editorial labels.

Keep people, products, materials, lighting, and reflections realistic and polished.

The final image should feel like a finished campaign key visual — bold, colorful, layered, and conceptually clear.

Avoid generic subject + big text layouts, random deformation, heavy 3D lettering, meaningless filler text, excessive UI graphics, clutter, and disconnected visual effects.

prompts.text:
MiniMax H3 Prompt
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is A from <Picture 1>, who teleports to intimidate B and unexpectedly lands seated.
<Subject 2> is B from <Picture 2>, who anticipates A's return and prepares a chair.
Preserve exact reference faces, hairstyles, costumes, accessories, colors, proportions and drawing styles. Keep equal standing heights, excluding ornaments.
<Audio 1> supplies the voice timbre and natural pitch range of <Subject 1> (S1). Use its vocal identity, never its recorded words. B is silent; leave any B voice reference unused.
summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] A 15-second Japanese 2D anime action-comedy. A teleports between two positions to show off. B calmly places a chair at A's next destination. A reappears in a low combat stance and unexpectedly settles onto the seat. B hands her tea. End on A's familiar silent, stunned face, now seated and holding a teacup. Use the selected aspect ratio.
retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (Shots 1-3): fully_preserved - reference identity and design, new actions.
<Subject 2> (Shots 1-2): fully_preserved - reference identity and design, new actions.
<Audio 1>: reference - A's single opening line.
Images define appearance and style, not poses, backgrounds or reference-sheet layouts.
detailed_description:
High-quality hand-drawn 2D anime, clean linework, cel shading, fluid movement and expressive faces. A quiet stone courtyard in daylight. Exactly two people: one A and one B. B stands near screen-center. A uses two clear destinations on either side of B, each about two meters away. Both destinations lie at the same camera depth on level paving.
A faces mostly toward camera, head turned toward B. Each arrival uses the same low combat stance: knees bent, feet apart, torso upright, hips at chair-seat height, right hand extended. Keep this orientation for the final arrival.

A fully disappears before reappearing elsewhere. The old position becomes empty. Only ONE A is ever visible. Use abstract violet sparks, never clones, human-shaped trails, ghosts or split screens.
Establish one wooden chair beside B and a small table behind her, holding one white teacup and saucer. The chair has four legs, solid seat and low backrest. Props retain their designs and scale; none appear magically.

[Shot 1] Open on a locked wide full-body shot, showing both teleport destinations, B and the furniture. A begins at the screen-left destination, chair still beside B.
During 0.3-2.8 seconds, <Subject 1> (S1), using <Audio 1>'s voice timbre, confidently declares, [Japanese] このうごきに、ついてこれるか! Synchronize her lips with this one sentence and finish before three seconds. She drops into her low combat pose, smiling smugly.
At about three seconds, A vanishes completely from the left in a brief violet shimmer. After a short empty interval, the SAME A appears at the right destination in the same stance. Her original position stays empty. Use a crisp magical whoosh. B turns only her eyes and head to follow.
At about four and a half seconds, A disappears fully from the right and reappears at the left in the same pose. Clearly show the right destination empty afterward. B tracks her without surprise.
[Shot 2] At 00:05.000, cut to a slightly closer, stable wide shot that still includes both destinations, both characters and the furniture. Hold this shot continuously through chair placement, the final arrival and the tea handoff.

A disappears from the left and appears on the right once more. While A poses proudly on the right, B grips the chair's backrest with both hands and slides it into the now-empty left destination. Show all four chair legs moving over the paving. No cut or flash conceals the placement.
The chair faces toward camera, matching A's established arrival stance. Its seat is centered directly beneath the position where A's hips will appear. Its backrest stands behind that position and does not intersect her body. B finishes placing it, releases it and steps clear before A returns.

Around seven and a half seconds, A completely disappears from the right. Briefly show the empty right destination and the waiting chair on the left. Then A materializes just above the chair seat in her usual bent-knee combat pose, with her feet on either side of the chair's front legs.

Her hips appear just above the seat, back clear of the backrest. Finishing her stance, she settles onto the seat with a small bounce. No body part intersects the stationary chair.

Stop the dramatic music exactly when she sits. Use a modest wooden creak, not an impact crash. A is now seated with her right hand still extended in the same grand fighting gesture. She did not choose to sit and has not yet understood what happened. Hold this absurd pose briefly.

Between nine and eleven seconds, B picks up the cup and saucer from the nearby table: left hand supports the saucer, right hand steadies the cup. She presents them at A's chest height. A absentmindedly relaxes her combat gesture to accept the tea, supporting the saucer with her left hand and taking the cup handle with her right.

Show the handoff continuously. B releases after A has a secure grip. A holds the cup above the saucer without drinking. No duplication, spills or floating props.

B straightens beside the chair, quietly satisfied. A looks down at the tea, then realizes that her intimidating attack has turned into a seated tea break. No further teleportation.

[Shot 3] At 00:12.000, cut to a frontal chest-up view of seated A. Include the cup and saucer near the lower frame edge and the chair back behind her to preserve the visual joke. B remains outside this framing.

A looks up from the tea. Her eyes widen, pupils become small and eyebrows lift. Her lips part slightly once, then stay still. Use her familiar stunned, uncomprehending expression. No blush, crying, anger or exaggerated panic.

Slowly push in; hold the final full second on her silent face, hands steady around the tea. End on A, with no drinking, standing, new attack or extra gag.

overall_soundscape:
Exactly one spoken sentence, by A in Shot 1. B never vocalizes. After three seconds, no dialogue, narration, gasps, grunts, screams, laughter or vocal breaths.
Use short distinct teleport whooshes, a light chair scrape, a wooden creak as A sits and a soft ceramic clink during the handoff. Keep quiet courtyard ambience beneath the final pause.

non_diegetic_music:
Fast, serious instrumental action music accompanies A's teleport display. Stop abruptly when her hips meet the chair. No music afterward. No choir, vocal samples, comedy sting or canned laughter.

No text, subtitles, logos, watermarks, HUD, extra characters, clones, afterimages, simultaneous copies of A, extra chairs or teacups, body intersections, extra limbs or fingers, fused hands, changing character scale, costume redesign, injury, photorealism, 3D rendering or chibi redesign.

Prompt:

TITLE: [your title]
SUBJECT: [person + pose]
DISTORTION: [echo / scan / motion delay / type refraction]
PALETTE: [neutral base + one accent]
FORMAT: 9:16

Create a premium fashion editorial portrait using controlled vertical slit-scan distortion.

Begin with a strong realistic portrait and keep at least one clear identity anchor such as the eyes, profile or facial outline. Break selected areas into vertical slices with varied widths, compression and horizontal displacement, creating a gradual transition from clear photography to optical fragmentation.

Keep some areas completely sharp rather than distorting the whole image. Preserve realistic skin, hair and fabric texture inside every slice.

Use a restrained palette, strong silhouette and generous negative space. Keep typography clean and editorial: one title, one short phrase and minimal supporting copy.

The result should feel like an optical photography experiment and high-fashion magazine poster, not a digital glitch effect.

Avoid RGB splitting, VHS noise, horizontal scanlines, uniform slices, neon cyberpunk graphics, excessive text, plastic skin, logos, numbering and watermarks.

prompts.label: 完整提示词
prompts.text:
Prompt:

Create a 9:16 editorial collage poster built around a fan-shaped composition.

SUBJECT: [your theme / subject]
TITLE: [main title]
CONCEPT: [what the composition should express]
FAN STRUCTURE: [fragmented burst / rounded fan pages / diagonal collage / constructivist radial / custom variation]
VISUAL MATERIALS: [portrait photography / botanical specimens / architecture / objects / archival images / textures]
COLOR SYSTEM: [2–5 dominant colors]
TYPOGRAPHY: [editorial serif / grotesk / condensed sans / other]
BACKGROUND: [paper tone / flat color]
TEXT DETAILS: [optional short meaningful phrases]

Treat the fan shape as the main visual system, not as a decorative frame. Build one strong large-scale silhouette first, then place rich visual information inside or around it.

Do not default to evenly spaced straight wedges. The fan structure may be irregular, curved, rounded, fragmented, asymmetrical, layered, partially broken, or constructed from mechanical lines depending on the concept.

Let the geometry carry meaning:

* fragmented shapes can suggest media, memory or visual overload
* rounded fan pages can suggest growth, nature or unfolding
* diagonal sections can create tension and narrative movement
* precise radial lines can suggest systems, architecture or construction

Combine photography, cropped details, textures, linework, flat color fields and negative space with clear hierarchy. Some sections may contain dense imagery, while others should remain pure color or empty space to create rhythm.

Use bold cropping, scale shifts and a few controlled elements crossing the fan boundaries so the composition feels designed rather than like photos placed inside containers.

Keep the color palette intentional and sectional. Each major area should have a clear color identity without becoming visually noisy.

Typography should feel integrated into an art poster or independent editorial publication. Use one clear title and only a small amount of meaningful supporting text. Avoid placeholder copy, excessive labels, UI-style information boxes or random tiny text.

The finished image should work at two distances:
from far away, the fan-shaped structure is immediately recognizable and visually striking;
up close, the viewer discovers layered photography, materials, details and narrative meaning.

Aim for experimental editorial design, art-poster quality, strong thumbnail impact and high information density without clutter.

Prompt:

CORE WORD: [e.g. ORBIT / PORTAL / VANISH / DEPTH]
PROJECT NAME: [brand / exhibition / campaign name]
SPATIAL STRUCTURE: [spiral ramp / nested frames / tunnel / layered panels / other]
SCENE: [architectural environment]
SUBJECT: [small human figure / cyclist / none]
MAIN COLOR: [one strong accent color]
SUPPORTING TEXT: [date / location / short tagline]
FORMAT: 9:16 vertical poster

Create a contemporary perspective typography poster where oversized type becomes part of the physical space instead of simply sitting on top of the image.

Build one clear spatial system first, then make the typography strictly follow its geometry, perspective, curvature, depth and surface changes.

The main word should occupy roughly 35–55% of the composition and act as the primary visual structure.

Depending on the chosen spatial structure, allow the letterforms to:

* wrap around curved architecture,
* continue across floors and walls,
* pass through repeated frames,
* or split across multiple depth layers and visually realign from one specific viewpoint.

The typography must feel physically integrated into the environment, with correct scale, perspective, occlusion and surface contact. From the intended camera angle, the word should remain recognizable and visually powerful even if individual letterforms are distorted by the architecture.

Use a restrained palette with one strong accent color against neutral concrete, black, white or architectural materials. Keep the color fields clean, solid and graphic rather than glossy, neon or heavily textured.

If a person is included, keep them relatively small and use them as a scale reference. They should naturally walk, ride or move through the typographic space rather than pose for the camera.

Add only a small amount of secondary editorial information such as project name, location, date and one short thematic line. Keep it clearly subordinate to the main word.

Overall style: experimental typography, spatial graphic design, contemporary architecture, editorial poster, installation art, strong depth, clean hierarchy, high-impact composition.

Her hair is exceptionally long, dense, and naturally black. Because she is already lying flat, the hair explodes outward above and beside her head, producing a huge irregular black silhouette that resembles a chaotic halo. Do not make the hair form a clean circle. Preserve crossing strands, loose loops, tangles, flyaways, uneven edges, and tiny cool highlights created by the flash. Some notes rest beside her hair, across the shoulders and torso, over the abdomen, and near the legs. Keep the layout messy rather than graphic or symmetrical. Several notes may visibly resemble motion-picture prop money instead of being presented as verified real cash. Near the very top of the frame, scatter a smaller number of transparent or pale-blue acrylic pieces that visually resemble broken glass, adding to the chaotic party-installation feeling. The lower garment is only partially seen: simple black or very dark navy shorts or another very short dark bottom with a pale or white waistband edge. Do not invent elaborate clothing details.  Keep her adult body slim and elongated but realistically proportioned. The waist can be naturally defined, never aggressively cinched. Visible skin includes the face, ears, neck, collarbones, shoulders, both arms and hands, parts of the upper arms, midriff, and a large foreground section of thigh and knee. Use a light cool-neutral to lightly warm-neutral ivory complexion, with stronger peach-pink flush across the cheeks. The skin should visually suggest a soft, fine, clean, slightly cool tactile quality somewhere between powdery matte and natural satin. Preserve tiny pores, subtle arm texture, knee coloration, minute tonal variation, and slight abdominal surface changes. Preserve the reference's softly narrow facial proportions, refined jawline, almond-shaped eyes, natural nose proportions, and full but restrained lips without replacing her with any specific celebrity.  She looks straight upward into the camera with a calm, slightly tired, self-contained gaze. Her lips remain naturally closed or only faintly relaxed apart, without a clear smile. The expression should feel like someone who is completely aware of being photographed after the party has already happened, yet is not trying too hard to perform for the camera.  The most important gesture is one arm reaching aggressively upward toward the camera while offering a single banknote. Because the camera uses a close wide-angle viewpoint, preserve dramatic foreshortening: the hand, thumb, and bill should appear significantly larger than the face. Since the hand is extremely close to the lens, the nearest fingers and banknote may fall slightly out of focus and become slightly brighter or even mildly clipped by the flash. Do not correct this distortion. The other hand should cross the chest or abdomen while still moving, leaving a subtle motion smear that makes the photograph feel caught mid-action rather than completely frozen.  Layer multiple pearl necklaces with thin metallic chains around the neck. Allow one longer pearl strand to fall naturally across the black crop top, bending and overlapping beneath scattered bills. Add several fine rings to the fingers and a silver watchband, watch, or stack of metallic bracelets to the opposite wrist. The pearls and metal should catch tiny sharp white points of direct-flash reflection.  Photographically, emulate a smartphone rear wide camera or compact digital camera with near-axis direct flash, not a polished soft-lit studio setup. Use approximately a 24–35mm full-frame-equivalent perspective, with the camera roughly 0.8–1.3 meters above the body, in a tall vertical frame close to 3:5. Fire a strong direct flash almost exactly along the optical axis at around 5200–6000K. Let the flash dominate the scene: produce bright direct highlights on the forehead, nose, cheeks, arms, abdomen and thigh, while creating short, relatively defined shadows beneath the nose, chin, fingers, pearl strands and body edges.  The white bedding and pale paper should bounce part of the flash back into the subject, keeping the harder shadows from becoming completely black. At the same time, preserve very deep blacks in the hair and clothing, producing a strong graphic contrast against the almost blown-white bedding. The foreground hand, being closest to the flash, may appear brighter than the face and slightly overexposed.  Do not over-clean the photograph. Preserve direct-flash digital sharpening, a small amount of noise and social-media compression, uneven brightness across the white bedding, foreground softness, tiny blown highlights, motion trails, wrinkled sheets, randomly folded bills, chaotic hair, and slightly off-center framing. The face and torso should remain relatively crisp, while the nearest fingers and bill may be softer; most background notes should remain readable rather than disappearing into heavy bokeh.  She had already fallen into the scattered bills, and her hair had already spread across the bed. Several notes had landed on her body. Now she is pushing one directly toward the camera, while the other hand is still finishing its movement. A second later, that hand might cover the lens completely or throw the bill back onto the bed.  The final image should combine Y2K flash photography, alt-fashion, luxury parody, money-bed editorial imagery, and a private after-party bedroom snapshot. Keep it cool, visually excessive, slightly absurd, playfully boastful, and imperfect. It should feel like a real human being was suddenly photographed with direct flash—not like a pristine luxury campaign or a flawlessly polished AI render.

Prompt:

[POSTER THEME]: {fill in the theme}
[MAIN TITLE]: {fill in the title}
[TOP SECTION]: {portrait / object archive / typography / image}
[MIDDLE SECTION]: {information band / typography / image / transition}
[BOTTOM SECTION]: {landscape / hero object / second portrait / typography}
[COLOR PALETTE]: {fill in the palette}
[VISUAL STYLE]: {editorial / museum / photography exhibition / cultural poster}
[ASPECT RATIO]: 9:16

Create a sophisticated vertical editorial poster built around a clear three-part composition: top, middle, and bottom.

Each section must have a distinct visual role, but the final poster should feel like one continuous design rather than three stacked rectangular panels.

Use strong differences in scale, image density, typography, and negative space to establish hierarchy.

The top section should create the first visual anchor through a bold image, oversized typography, or a strong subject.

The middle section should act as the structural hinge of the composition. It can use a title, information field, narrow panoramic image, color band, or typography layer to connect the upper and lower sections.

The bottom section should provide a second visual weight or spatial conclusion through a landscape, object, secondary portrait, or oversized type.

Avoid rigid card-like boundaries. Let selected elements cross between sections through masking, overlap, irregular silhouettes, transparency, atmospheric transitions, foreground/background relationships, or typography extending beyond its original area.

Typography must actively participate in the composition rather than simply sit on top of the image. Allow large letterforms to be cropped by the page, partially hidden behind subjects, overlap imagery, or interact with negative space.

Use a strong editorial hierarchy:
one dominant title,
one clear secondary information layer,
and small meaningful metadata such as dates, venue, category, or curatorial text.

Small text should feel like real exhibition or editorial information, not decorative filler.

Keep some areas intentionally quiet. Do not fill every empty space.

The first read should communicate the main visual structure immediately.
The second read should reveal the interaction between type and imagery.
The third read should reveal the smaller information and details.

Maintain a refined contemporary poster aesthetic with strong typography, deliberate cropping, controlled information density, clean print texture, and professional editorial spacing.

Prompt:

TITLE: [TENSION / DRIFT / FOCUS / REFRACT / your own word]
PROJECT: [brand / exhibition / campaign name]
ENVIRONMENT: [fabric canopy / terrain / mirror installation / water / other]
TYPE MECHANISM: [surface distortion / terrain warp / reflection / refraction]
SUBJECT: [small human figure / none]
MAIN COLOR: [accent color]
FORMAT: 9:16 vertical poster

Create a contemporary perspective typography poster where oversized type is physically transformed by the material or environment around it.

The main word should occupy roughly 35–55% of the composition and become part of the scene itself. Let the letterforms stretch, bend, split, compress or realign according to the chosen surface or optical medium.

For fabric, let the type follow tension, curvature and suspended folds.
For terrain, let it wrap across slopes, ridges and valleys.
For mirrors, distort the source typography so the reflection resolves into a readable word.
For water, use depth and refraction to shift and reconnect the letterforms.

Keep the spatial logic physically believable, with correct perspective, occlusion, reflections, refraction and surface contact.

Use one strong accent color against a restrained architectural or natural palette. Keep the typography bold, clean and highly legible from the intended viewpoint.

If a person is included, keep them small and use them mainly as a scale reference or observer within the typographic space.

Add only a small amount of secondary editorial information such as project name, date, location and one short thematic line.

Overall style: perspective typography, spatial graphic design, contemporary installation art, editorial poster, strong depth, clean hierarchy and high visual impact.

What happens when your dinner is ten times bigger than you.

Prompt: 
Use my uploaded portrait/selfie as the ONLY identity and facial reference. Preserve my recognizable facial identity and appearance naturally.

Vertical top-down food-photography image with an absurdist scale premise: a woman with the face from the reference photo, at dinner-guest scale, lies on her back inside a large white ceramic plate heaped with steamed white rice, cradling a whole grilled fish across her chest with both arms as if hugging a plush toy, looking straight up into the camera with a completely neutral serious expression — that seriousness is what makes the joke work. Wardrobe (womenswear): a red-and-cream abstract-print bomber jacket with a spread collar, dropped shoulders and elasticated cuffs, worn open; a plain cream oversized t-shirt underneath; layered silver bead chain necklaces; a red leather belt with a squared silver buckle; extremely wide-leg knee-length cow-print shorts in brown and cream; tall white ribbed crew socks; honey-tan lace-up work boots; and an embroidered patterned trucker cap worn straight. Camera: pure overhead, lens perpendicular to the tabletop, medium focal length with minimal distortion visible only at the plate rim which reads slightly elliptical rather than perfectly circular — that 90-degree angle flattens the scene so the human figure and the food occupy the same visual plane without perspective conflict, which is what makes the composite possible. Composition: the white plate is a circle containing everything and filling almost the whole frame; the figure laid along a soft diagonal from upper center down to lower left, the fish crossing it on the opposite diagonal to form an X; a spoon at the left and a fork at the right acting as symmetrical vertical brackets; splashed sauce droplets scattered around breaking the symmetry and adding movement. Lighting: a large diffused source from the upper left — window or wide softbox — producing soft short shadows thrown by the fish onto the rice toward the right, open fill on the right side of the face, and elongated speculars along the fish skin, the cutlery metal and the silver chains; no hard shadows, no backlight, standard culinary lighting built to describe texture. Texture and detail: rice defined grain by grain, the fish showing cracked golden skin with an oil sheen, sauce with real viscosity in droplets of varying size and pinpoint reflections, crisp fried onion strands keeping their crunch, plus broccoli, sliced carrot, green beans and red chilli scattered through the rice and a spoonful of red chilli paste at the left. Include convincing contact shadows and a few grains of rice overlapping the edges of her sleeves and shorts so the figure sits inside the food rather than on top of it. Surroundings on the wooden table: two glasses of iced dark soda at the top corners, a bowl of apples and mango at the upper left, a lime wedge at the lower right, and warm orange-brown wood grain visible around the plate. Grade: warm and saturated, amber in the sauce, red pushed hard in the jacket and belt, orange-brown in the wood; medium contrast, rice and plate whites controlled without clipping, lifted blacks, moderate added sharpening and fine grain. Palette: white rice and plate dominating absolutely and rhyming with the cream tee and socks, amber and brown of the sauce, fish, cow-print shorts and boots forming the warm central mass, saturated red jacket and belt as the accent placed at the exact center, silver cutlery and chains as the metallic notes, and scattered greens and oranges from the vegetables as points of colour.

提示词：

做一张 9:16 竖版东方文化艺术海报，核心方法是“强主体 + 巨型野字 + 明确动势”。

背景使用干净温暖的象牙白艺术纸，保留轻微纸张纹理。不要复杂背景，不要脏污做旧，不要模板化排版，让大面积留白成为画面的一部分。

画面里使用两个超大的黑色毛笔字作为主要视觉骨架。书法要粗重、野性、自由，带明显提按、飞白和真实墨迹边缘。两个字不要排得太工整，可以错位、压叠、上下呼应，部分笔画直接出画。

在画面中央放置一个强主体器物，主体必须足够大、轮廓足够清楚，并且有真实体积、材质和结构。主体可以是纸鸢、大鼓、折扇、长刃，或其他具有强识别度的东方器物。

最重要的是，让主体和野字发生一个一眼就能看懂的动态关系。不要只是把器物摆在字前面，而是让主体真正改变文字：可以破框、冲击、放射、斜切、拉开、穿插、推动，或者让笔画随着主体的方向和力量发生变化。

整体构图要有一条非常明确的动势线。可以是斜向破框、放射展开、正面冲击，或一条强烈的切割轴。让观众一眼就感到画面在“动”，而不是静态陈列。

版式上采用非对称编辑设计。中央区域负责“强主体 + 巨型野字 + 动势关系”，左右边缘再加入小尺寸展览信息、日期、地点和材质说明，让画面既有视觉冲击，也有文化展览海报的出版感。

加入少量自然手写英文标题，像设计师后来补上的注释。英文不要太大，主要起到节奏调节作用。可以再加入极少量朱红印章作为点缀，但不要堆太多装饰元素。

整体配色控制为暖象牙白、深墨黑，再加一个主体本身的主色。比如纸鸢可带少量朱砂红，大鼓可用深红鼓身，折扇可用米白加红刷痕，长刃则以冷银灰为主。颜色不要太杂。

最终效果要像高完成度的东方展览海报：主体够强，字够野，方向够明确，画面张力直接拉满。适合传统工艺、东方文化和展览视觉这类海报参考。

避免人物、普通产品广告、电商摆拍、国潮插画、红金节庆感、霓虹科技感、廉价 CGI，以及无意义的墨点堆积。
